attorneys.name: Gregory M. Funfsinn
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Like his political and legal hero, Abraham Lincoln, Greg Funfsinn comes from humble beginnings. Greg was born in the small farm town of Mendota, Illinois - home of the National Sweet Corn Festival - and raised on his family's farm in Bureau County, Illinois. Greg's dad worked for 47 years at a Caterpillar factory outside of Mendota and even longer on the family farm, before finally retiring. His mom was primarily a stay-at-home mom raising Greg and his two siblings, but also worked on-and-off over the years as a receptionist, waitress, and at an insurance agency before eventually retiring.

Greg graduated near the top of his class from Mendota Township High School and then attended Loyola University Chicago. He was the first in his family to go to college. Greg paid his way through college with some help from his parents, a lot of help from student loans, and also by working a few summers in a factory and doing retail work during the school year. Greg graduated with a Bachelor's Degree in Criminal Justice. Greg's interest in law enforcement and his love of investigating almost took him to the FBI or into policing, but instead took him to law school. During the year between college and law school, Greg worked as a project assistant at Vedder Price, an international business-focused law firm in Chicago.

Greg then enrolled in law school at Chicago-Kent College of Law. He graduated with his law degree and after graduation began working for the Cook County State's Attorney's Office (CCSAO) as a criminal prosecutor. The CCSAO is the 2nd largest prosecutors' office in the United States. Greg began his career as an Assistant State's Attorney in the Appeals Division, where he honed his ability to conduct legal research and formulate persuasive legal arguments in writing. He argued multiple cases in the Illinois Court of Appeals and wrote nearly 35 appellate briefs. After years in the Appeals Division, he was promoted to the 4th District Criminal Trial Division. During his time in the trial division, Greg handled more than 100 bench trials, several jury trials, and hundreds of court hearings.

Since moving to Lexington, Greg worked for several years at two well-respected law firms in Kentucky. He has represented individuals and businesses involved in a wide variety of lawsuits. Greg has participated in hundreds of depositions, numerous court hearings and oral arguments, and several jury trials. When he's not practicing law or spending time with his family, Greg enjoys volunteering for Lexington Habitat for Humanity and playing sports. He was a member of the 2014 Class of Leadership Kentucky and the 2018-19 Class of Leadership Lexington.

With the founding of Hicks & Funfsinn, PLLC, Greg will use his vast experience and knowledge in handling injury claims and litigating injury lawsuits for individuals just like you.

attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
When going through a divorce or family law matter, it is important to have a dedicated attorney at your side to guide you through the process with compassion. Anthony Galasso is a committed Senior Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm. Based in our Louisville, Kentucky office, he is prepared to represent clients in Jefferson County and surrounding areas.

Anthony attended the University of Kentucky College of Law in Lexington, Kentucky, where he earned his Juris Doctor in 2011. While working towards his degree, Anthony held roles as a document review paralegal, law clerk, and legal research assistant. Prior to law school, he attended the University of Richmond in Richmond, Virginia, where he received a Bachelor of Arts in 2007.

Before joining the Louisville divorce and family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Anthony most recently served as a Senior Claims Analyst, adjusting claims for real estate errors and omissions insurance claims. Before that, he worked as an Associate Attorney focusing on insurance litigation. In that role, he litigated health insurance, workers’ compensation, and property and casualty subrogation cases nationwide. His earlier experience includes positions across Kentucky as a Conflicts Staff Attorney, Associate Attorney, and Subrogation Attorney. Throughout his legal history, Anthony has developed strong research, analyzation, and negation skills. With these skills and his vast legal experience, Anthony is equipped to represent you in your family law matter.

attorneys.name: Peter M. Gannott
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Peter M. Gannott's (PMG) law practice focuses on three main areas: (1) business and consumer bankruptcy; (2) creditors' rights and commercial collect litigation; and (3) complex commercial, business, and real estate litigation.

Mr. Gannott's bankruptcy experience includes involvement in Chapter 7, Chapter 11 and Chapter 13 bankruptcies. He has represented debtors, secured and unsecured creditors, unsecured creditors' committees and has acted as lead counsel for Chapter 7 and Chapter 11 Trustees. His experience includes representing banks, trade creditors, equipment lessors and landlords. He has litigated disclosure statements, reorganization plans, preferences, fraudulent conveyances, priorities, breaches of fiduciary duties, guarantees, mortgage and lien enforcement and perfection, Uniform Commercial Code questions, stay relief motions and adequate protection issues. Mr. Gannott has handled bankruptcies pending in Kentucky, Indiana, Ohio, Missouri, Illinois, Florida, Kansas, Michigan, Texas and Colorado. He has litigated these proceedings before the bankruptcy and district courts and argued bankruptcy issues before the Sixth Circuit and Seventh Circuit courts of appeals.

During Mr. Gannott's thirty-five (35) years of legal experience, he has been lead-counsel for numerous jury trials, bench trials and appeals before both state and federal courts. He is currently licensed to practice law in the state courts of Kentucky and Indiana, and is admitted before ten district courts, three circuit courts and the U.S. Supreme Court.

As a frequent lecturer, Mr. Gannott speaks in the areas of bankruptcy, creditors' rights and real estate. He graduated with Honors from the University of Illinois with degrees in History and Political Science and obtained his law degree from the Washington College of Law, American University, in Washington, D.C.

attorneys.name: Jonathon C. Garnett
attorneys.firm_name: Crow Estate Planning and Probate, PLC
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Hopkinsville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised on a family farm in Hopkinsville, Kentucky, my journey to the law is deeply connected with my roots. Growing up, I never really worked a traditional job like many of my friends did. Rather I grew up working on our family farm, where my parents still live and work today. Two of the most important qualities passed from one generation to the next in many working families are determination and integrity. Pursuing a career centered around estate planning will allow me to help these same families not only pass down strong character traits, but to also preserve a lasting legacy for future generations.

Although dedication to my legal work is crucial, I enjoy spending time with my family and friends whenever possible. To date, I have traveled across Europe, walked along the beaches of Hawaii, and hiked several miles in Glacier National Park with my friends and family. As a part of an active family, I enjoy both water and snow skiing, and spend quality time doing both each year.

While I have enjoyed spending time with different people, my favorite person to make memories with is my wife, Maci. We met at WKU where we fell in love before moving to Lexington where I attended law school. Some of our favorite hobbies include cheering on the Kentucky Wildcats, cooking dinner together and spending time with our Australian Shepherd, Harper.

I began my education at Western Kentucky University, graduating in 2020 with a Bachelor’s of Science in Economics and minored in Finance. I joined Sigma Chi Fraternity and was selected as a Spirit Master, which served as an official ambassador for the Office of The University President. During my time at WKU, I also worked for United Southern Bank over the summer.

After graduating from WKU, I attended the University of Kentucky for law school. I was a member of the Federalist Society, and during my summers, I interned with Crow Estate Planning and Probate as well as Bluegrass Land Title in Lexington. I believe these previous experiences allowed me to immerse myself into the world of legacy and succession planning.

Upon graduating in 2024, I was happy to accept a full-time position with my previous internship here at Crow, and will serve the greater Hopkinsville area as well as our Tennessee clients with their estate planning and probate matters. I look forward to meeting you and would love to craft a plan that fits your unique situation!

Some of our favorite hobbies include cheering on the Kentucky Wildcats, cooking dinner together and spending time with our Australian Shepherd, Harper.

I began my education at Western Kentucky University, graduating in 2020 with a Bachelor’s of Science in Economics and minored in Finance. I joined Sigma Chi Fraternity and was selected as a Spirit Master, which served as an official ambassador for the Office of The University President. During my time at WKU, I also worked for United Southern Bank over the summer.

After graduating from WKU, I attended the University of Kentucky for law school. I was a member of the Federalist Society, and during my summers, I interned with Crow Estate Planning and Probate as well as Bluegrass Land Title in Lexington. I believe these previous experiences allowed me to immerse myself into the world of legacy and succession planning.

Upon graduating in 2024, I was happy to accept a full-time position with my previous internship here at Crow, and will serve the greater Hopkinsville area as well as our Tennessee clients with their estate planning and probate matters. I look forward to meeting you and would love to craft a plan that fits your unique situation!

content: On September 13, 2023, obtained a $100,000 jury verdict (the maximum amount requested by plaintiffs) in Ermold v. Davis, United States District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 0:15-cv-00046-DLB-EBA. The sole claim at issue in this action was against Kim Davis (the then-Clerk of Rowan County, Kentucky) under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 for violating plaintiffs’ rights under the United States Constitution when she refused to issue this same-sex couple a marriage license.
Obtained a summary judgment against Kim in Ermold v. Davis, 2022 WL 830606 (E.D. Ky. Mar. 18, 2022).

Obtained a reversal before the Court of Appeals of Kentucky of an order granting judgment on the pleadings that an assignment of claims was champertous and thus invalid in THC Kentucky Coal Venture I LLC v. Richard, 2020 WL 4512817 (Ky. Ct. App. July 24, 2020).

Successfully prosecuted a motion to hold JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. in contempt of court for violating the discharge injunction in a Chapter 13 bankruptcy case of In re Van Pelt, 599 B.R. 1 (E.D. Bankr. 2019).

Obtained a reversal at the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit of an order denying summary judgment for the plaintiff on a claim for contract reformation in First Tech. Capital, Inc. v. Airborne, Inc., 726 F. App’x 85 (2d Cir. 2018).

Successfully defended an appeal before the Supreme Court of Kentucky of a $1,308,403.60 judgment entered against an oil and gas producer for failure to pay natural gas royalties in Nami Resources Company, L.L.C. v. Asher Land and Mineral, Ltd., 554 S.W.3d 323 (Ky. 2018)

Obtained a reversal at the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit of the trial court’s dismissal of claims against Kim Davis (the then-Clerk of Rowan County) in her individual and official capacities for her refusal to issue a marriage license to a same-sex couple in Ermold v. Davis, 855 F.3d 715 (6th Cir. 2017).

In October 2015, obtained as lead counsel for twenty-one plaintiffs at a thirteen-hour mediation a confidential settlement against Fifth Third Bank less than three weeks before a scheduled three-week jury trial before the Fayette Circuit Court in a civil action styled as CPC Livestock, LLC v. Fifth Third Bank, Civil No. 13-CI-03666. Plaintiffs’ asserted tort claims totaled approximately $7.8 million.

In October 2014, obtained as lead counsel for counterclaim-defendants a summary judgment on $5.1 million of asserted counterclaims for breach of contract, fraud, negligent misrepresentation and unjust enrichment in First Technology Capital, Inc. v. JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., 53 F. Supp. 3d 972 (E.D. Ky. 2014).
Created new law in the First Circuit as to the interpretation of Rule 60(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure in Crowe v. Bolduc, 365 F.3d 86 (1st Cir. 2004).

Successfully defended a federal class action that raised a liability issue of first impression concerning the intersection of bankruptcy law and Maine law governing the failure to pay severance pay. Carrier v. JPB Enters., No. 01-187-P-C, 2001 WL 1646673 (D. Me. Dec. 26, 2001).
Collected $2.0 million from Mary Alice Davis, the heiress to the Shaw’s supermarket chain, in a Maine case that received significant local press coverage, both in newspapers and on television.

Briefed and argued an appeal to the Supreme Judicial Court of Maine concerning where the statute of limitations as to a city’s claim for unpaid property taxes was tolled during the client’s Chapter 7 bankruptcy proceeding in City of Saco v. Pulsifer, 749 A.2d 153 (Me. 2000).
Briefed and argued one of the most often-cited parol evidence cases decided under Maine law in Handy Boat Serv., Inc. v. Prof’l Servs., Inc., 711 A.2d 1306 (Me. 1998)
Negotiated transaction documents for the sale of substantially all the assets of Optical Dynamics Corporation for $1.4 million in its assignment for the benefit of creditors’ proceeding

Lead counsel for plaintiff in a multi-million dollar coal lease dispute in West Virginia Mid Vol, Inc. v. Rockhouse Land LLC (In re Hopedale Mining LLC), Adv. Proc. No. 1:20-bk-12043 (GRH). The litigation settled after a thirteen hour mediation in November 2021. As a result of the settlement, the client acquired the right to mine millions of tons of metallurgical coal located in West Virginia.

Successfully defended and settled in January 2010 an action styled Covol Fuels No. 3, LLC v. Redbird Mountain Coal Co., LLC, Adv. Case No. 09-6064 (Bankr. E.D. Ky.), in which the plaintiff sought $32.0 million of damages related to the construction of a coal processing facility on property owned by Asher Land and Mineral, LLLP. Through the settlement, Asher (the defendant client) received $2.8 million in the first quarter of 2010 and a favorable new long-term coal lease.

Lead litigation counsel for a plaintiff in a coal lease dispute involving millions of dollars in an adversary proceeding within the chapter 11 case of Horizon Natural Resources Company, one of the largest reorganization cases ever filed in the Eastern District of Kentucky. attorneys.name: Heather Gatnarek
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Advocacy Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Heather is a skilled litigator and trial attorney with over a decade of experience in both complex civil and criminal matters. She utilizes her background to help guide clients through all phases of commercial disputes from the commonplace to the most complex.

Heather began her career at the Kentucky Department of Public Advocacy’s Capital Trials Branch, where she represented indigent Kentuckians facing capital charges. Her representation spanned from arraignment through pre-trial litigation and preparation to trial or settlement. She then joined the ACLU of Kentucky, where she investigated and litigated constitutional challenges to statutes, regulations, and government practices at all levels of Kentucky’s court system as well as federal trial and appellate courts. Heather also litigated Open Records cases, prosecuted putative class litigation, and provided regulatory compliance advice to clients.

Heather has vast courtroom experience, including representing parties at criminal and civil trials, and arguing appeals and motions in state and federal courts. Her strengths include her zealous advocacy, responsiveness to clients, and ability to distill complex legal matters down to their component parts. Clients benefit from her relentless litigation of constitutional and civil rights challenges and her passion for institutional change.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Kentucky Department of Public Advocacy Furman Award, 2019

attorneys.name: April Hollon Gatlin
attorneys.practice_type: Probate Lawyers in Covington, KY
attorneys.bio:
April Hollon Gatlin has a breadth of experience in various areas of the law including, probate, municipality, real estate, domestic, and, litigation. As a complex litigator and trial attorney, April has been lead attorney covering a wide range of matters including real estate, contract disputes, construction, leases, title disputes, felony defense, estates and insurance defense. As a domestic attorney, April has represented mothers and fathers in child support, custody, visitation, guardianship and adoptions. As a general practitioner, April has a unique understanding of the interplay between estate planning, probate and real estate and applies a multi-disciplinary approach to solving problems.

April previously served as Grant County Master Commissioner, overseeing hundreds of foreclosures per year. She served as a City Attorney for several Northern Kentucky cities and previously was a prosecutor handling adult jury trials and juvenile court.

April has always been very active in her community. She has served as both President of her local Kiwanis and Kindervelt chapters. She has also served as Secretary on the Holly Hill Board and was selected as a member of the Grant County Chamber of Commerce vision 2020.

April grew up on a dairy farm in Gravel Switch, Kentucky and showed many champion dairy cattle. Her time growing up on a farm in rural Kentucky taught her the value of hard work, honesty, and compassion toward others. As a proud mother of four children, April understands the challenges that face families in todays world. April resides in Union, Kentucky with her husband and law partner Jack Gatlin. Jack and April met their freshman year at the University of Kentucky and continued on together graduating from the University of Kentucky College of Law.

attorneys.name: Jack Gatlin
attorneys.practice_type: Small Business Law Lawyers in Covington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Jack focuses his practice in three main areas: complex litigation, municipal law, and representing family-owned and small businesses. He also possesses considerable experience in strategic business planning and consulting, as well as dispute resolution, holding certification as a mediator from Northern Kentucky University.

In his current role, Jack serves as the City Attorney for Erlanger, Dry Ridge, Independence, and Taylor Mill. He previously worked in the Grant County Attorney’s Office from 2003 to 2009, where he represented the Grant County Fiscal Court and was appointed Grant County Attorney in 2008. Jack has a strong record of representing municipalities across Kentucky and Ohio, particularly in planning, zoning, and litigation matters.

As a complex litigator and trial attorney, Jack has tried numerous jury cases in Ohio and Kentucky, advocating for businesses, banks, and individuals. He has taken the lead in a variety of cases, addressing issues such as multi-jurisdictional commercial disputes, contract disputes, construction litigation, shareholder and partner disagreements, breaches of fiduciary duty, fraud, residential, HUD, and commercial lease litigation, real estate and title disputes, major felony criminal defense, estate litigation including will contests, fire and theft losses, and environmental and toxic torts. Additionally, Jack has extensive experience in alternative dispute resolution, representing parties through the American Arbitration Association.

In his capacity as a small business attorney, Jack serves as general counsel to numerous small and mid-sized corporations. His expertise includes advising owners, executives, and officers on a wide range of business matters, including corporate formation, mergers and acquisitions, dissolution, succession planning, contract formation, compliance with government regulations, employment decisions, and property ownership and management.

Jack's work has garnered him various accolades, including recognition as a Rising Star in Ohio and Kentucky and as a Super Lawyer in Kentucky. He has received the highest AV rating from Martindale-Hubbell and a 10.0 rating from AVVO. A former Managing Partner of a regional law firm, Jack has also served as President of the Northern Kentucky Bar Association. Committed to community service, he has held board positions with the Grant County Tourism Commission, Dry Ridge Soup Kitchen, and Grant County Chamber Vision 2020. Furthermore, he has acted as Chairperson of the Grant County Joint Industrial Development Authority and Chairperson of the Cincinnati Real Estate Cooperative.

Jack is married to his law partner, April Gatlin. Together, they are raising four active children, one of whom is attending Thomas More University, another at the University of Kentucky, and the remaining two are deeply engaged in the arts. Jack and April first met at the University of Kentucky and share a mutual interest in attending sporting events, exploring nature, and spending quality time with their children.

attorneys.name: Ashley D. Gerughty
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Bowling Green, KY
attorneys.bio:
Ashley is an accomplished attorney specializing in estate planning, probate, business law, and creditor representation. With a reputation for providing personalized, strategic legal solutions, she is known for her expertise in guiding clients through complex legal matters. Ashley excels in all aspects of estate planning, from drafting wills and trusts to navigating probate procedures, ensuring smooth transitions, and the protection of financial legacies for individuals and families.

In addition to her work in estate planning, Ashley advises business owners on business structure formation, succession planning, and contract drafting, providing critical legal counsel to ensure long-term success and continuity. Her experience in creditor representation further strengthens her ability to handle a wide range of legal issues with precision.

Ashley’s legal insight is further enhanced by her active role in her community and her leadership within the legal profession. She currently serves on the Board of Directors for Junior Achievement of South-Central Kentucky, where she volunteers in local classrooms to inspire the next generation. She is also a member of the Probate and Trust Section of the Kentucky Bar Association and has previously served on the board of directors for the Warren County Bowling Green Bar Association.

Ashley is a former local representative for the Young Lawyers Division of the Kentucky Bar Association, and a 2015 graduate of the Leadership Bowling Green program, which reflects her ongoing commitment to personal and professional growth.

Ashley is dedicated to providing clear, practical, and effective legal solutions tailored to her clients' long-term objectives. Whether handling intricate estate matters or advising businesses through legal challenges, Ashley’s expertise and commitment to excellence make her a trusted advisor.

attorneys.name: John M. Ghaelian
attorneys.practice_type: Labor & Employment Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
John represents employers and management in connection with a variety of labor and employment matters, including the defense of state and federal government investigations and all types of discrimination, retaliation, harassment, and wage-and-hour claims in state and federal courts and administrative agencies. John also provides preventative advice and counsel to business owners, directors, upper management, and HR professionals on day-to-day personnel issues and leads internal investigations.

Prior to joining Lockaby PLLC, John served as General Counsel for the Kentucky Education and Labor Cabinet’s Department of Workplace Standards and Department of Workers’ Claims, where he led the Commonwealth’s legal teams investigating and prosecuting OSHA, wage-and-hour, and workers’ compensation violations. John also previously served as an Assistant Attorney General, working in the Office of Consumer Protection and Office of Medicaid Fraud and Abuse Control where he investigated and prosecuted a variety of civil fraud actions. John’s extensive experience with government investigations is second to none.

A native of Lexington, Kentucky, John attended Lafayette High School and received both his bachelor’s degree and law degree from the University of Kentucky. John is a member of the Kentucky Bar Association and serves on the Communications and Publications Committee. He is also a member of the Central Kentucky Inns of Court.

John enjoys traveling and has enjoyed visiting various countries in Western Europe and the Middle East. Further, he enjoys spending time with his spouse Jane and three kids Elizabeth, Charlie, and Leila.

attorneys.name: Colton W. Givens
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Bowling Green, KY
attorneys.bio:
Colton Givens joined Kerrick Bachert, PSC, in 2018. His practice focuses on civil litigation, encompassing insurance defense, business litigation, employment law, higher education law, and personal injury cases. Colton frequently appears in Kentucky's trial and appellate courts, handling both state and federal matters.

Colton previously worked as a law clerk for Judge Thomas B. Russell in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Kentucky and Judge Eugene E. Siler Jr. in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit before joining Kerrick Bachert, PSC.

Colton graduated summa cum laude from the University of Kentucky College of Law in 2016. He was a member of the Kentucky Law Journal editorial board and the school's National Trial Competition team. His student note was published in Volume 104 of the Kentucky Law Journal and received the Faculty Award for Outstanding Note. Colton earned his undergraduate degree in political science from Murray State University in 2013. During his time there, he participated in the mock trial team, marching band, and basketball pep band.

Colton has strong ties to South Central Kentucky. He was raised in Butler County and currently lives there.

attorneys.name: Matthew Gore
attorneys.practice_type: Personal injury Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Matthew Gore is a dedicated personal injury attorney at Colyer Law Firm. He has an unwavering commitment to upholding justice and advocating for the rights of individuals who have been wronged. He is a member of the Kentucky Bar, the Kentucky Justice Association, and the American Association for Justice. Whether in negotiation or litigation, he leverages his diverse experience and dedication to achieve the best possible outcomes for his clients.

Originally from West Virginia, Matthew earned his law degree from West Virginia University. He moved to the Shively neighborhood of Louisville in 2007 to be closer to family. He now considers Kentucky his adopted home. He has embraced the community and is committed to serving its residents with the highest level of legal care.

Prior to attending law school, Matthew worked for a Fortune 500 company where he gained valuable business experience. This background enriches his legal practice by providing him with a broad perspective on complex cases and a keen understanding of how to get the most compensation for his clients.

Before joining Colyer Law Firm, Matthew gained legal expertise as a defense attorney at a prominent Kentucky firm. This background gives him a comprehensive understanding of both sides of the legal process, allowing him to craft strategic and effective arguments for his clients. His transition to personal injury law was driven by a passion for helping those who have suffered due to the negligence of others, ensuring they receive the justice they deserve.

Matthew understands the profound impact that personal injuries can have on his clients' lives and works tirelessly to support them through every step of the legal process.

attorneys.name: David B. Gray
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
David Gray is the founder and principal attorney at Gray Law, bringing 36 years of experience in personal injury and medical malpractice law. He holds a bachelor’s degree in government and English from Centre College and earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Louisville School of Law. During his legal studies, David clerked for his uncle, Larry Franklin, contributing to numerous medical malpractice and personal injury cases.

Upon graduating from law school, David joined Franklin and Hance, where he practiced until 2000. He subsequently became a partner at Goldberg Simpson, serving until 2016 before establishing Gray Law.

Beyond his professional practice, David is committed to mentoring emerging attorneys and supporting lawyers facing alcohol or substance abuse challenges. He currently serves as vice chair of the board of Seven Counties Services and chairs the Kentucky Justice Association Wellness Committee. He regularly volunteers at the University of Louisville Brandeis School of Law, providing lectures and guidance to future legal professionals.

Outside of his legal career, Mr. Gray enjoys thoroughbred racing at Churchill Downs, culinary pursuits, boating, and spending time with his wife, Tracie, his daughters, Harper and Peyton, and his grandson, Brooks.

When she’s not representing clients, Peyton enjoys traveling, attending comedy shows, trying new restaurants, visiting with friends and family, and spending time at home with her husband, Alex, and two cats, Priss and Maisel.

attorneys.name: Michael R. Greene
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Michael R. Greene was born and raised in Louisville, Kentucky. Following his graduation from Saint Xavier High School, Michael attended the University of Kentucky. Following college, Michael returned home to Louisville to attend the Brandeis School of Law and obtained his law degree at the University of Louisville.

With a large portion of his career focused on personal injury, Michael has represented thousands of individuals and families who have suffered catastrophic injuries. With over 50 years of practicing law, Michael is qualified to handle your claims with efficiency, attention to detail and the highest level of personal service.

Since 1979, Michael has practiced as the senior partner in his firm, running his own firm. The founding of his firm was based upon two important principles. One, always treat the client with the utmost compassion and respect. Two, treat each case with the dedication and effort necessary to achieve the best possible result for the client. With over 35 years of practicing law with these twin aims, Michael has the ability to handle your case with compassion and dedication to ensure that the best possible outcome is achieved.

Michael is proud to have practiced law with his wife, Cynthia Greene for over 30 years. Together, Michael and Cynthia, are the proud parents of Joseph W. Greene, M.D., Wilson W. Greene, Sara Greene Diebold, M.D., and Daniel W. Greene. When not spending time with his family, Michael is an avid golfer and enjoys traveling.

attorneys.name: Wilson W. Greene
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Wilson Greene was born and raised in Louisville, Kentucky. Following his graduation from Saint Xavier High School, Wilson attended the College of Charleston located in Charleston, South Carolina. Following college, Wilson returned home to Louisville to attend the Brandeis School of Law at the University of Louisville. Immediately following the bar exam, Wilson began his legal career representing people who suffered severe personal injuries or death.

His first major case involved representing a wife who had lost her husband when he was killed in an automobile collision with an 18-wheeler. Since then, Wilson has focused a large portion of his career on heavy truck litigation, Wilson has represented numerous families who have lost loved ones as a result of commercial trucking collisions. Wilson has authored several articles used to educate other attorneys on how to effectively litigate heavy truck cases. Wilson is a member of the Association of Plaintiff Interstate Trucking Lawyers of America and has regularly been associated by attorneys in other states to handle cases involving commercial truck collisions. To the benefit of his clients, he has resolved multiple cases in excess of a million dollars. He has successfully achieved settlements or verdicts in commercial truck collisions throughout the southeast, including South Carolina, North Carolina, Alabama, and Kentucky.

In addition to his representation of individuals involved in commercial truck accidents, Wilson has recovered significant settlements and verdicts for individuals in a wide range of cases, including; automobile accidents, slip and falls, motorcycle accidents, workers' compensation claims, injuries from fires and explosions, permanent burns and scarring, bad faith claims against insurance companies, product liability claims, medical negligence, pharmaceutical litigation, rollover claims against automobile manufacturers, negligence by bars and restaurants for violating alcohol liability laws, failure to pay wages and commissions, and negligence actions against construction contractors for jobsite injuries and premises injuries.

Prior to founding The Greene Law Firm, PLLC, Wilson was an attorney with the Charleston, South Carolina law firm of Pierce, Herns, Sloan & McLeod, LLC where his practice included representing both Defendants and Plaintiffs. Early in his career, Wilson had the opportunity to work for a large insurance company defending automobile collisions and premises liability claims. This provided the unique opportunity to gain insight as to the tactics defense counsel utilize when evaluating and defending a case. The opportunity to work for an insurance company early in his career has been beneficial because now Wilson can utilize his experience and insider knowledge regarding defense tactics to his advantage while in litigation, negotiations, and trial.

attorneys.name: Peyton Griffee
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Shepherdsville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Peyton Holmes Porter Griffee serves as an attorney at the Sweat & Griffee Law Firm, in Shepherdsville, Kentucky, where he is a partner. Mr. Griffee and his wife Caitlin are longtime residents of Mount Washington, where he was born and raised. After completing his undergraduate studies at Georgetown University, he went on to earn his Juris Doctor at the University of Louisville's Brandeis School of Law.

Mr. Griffee participated in the National Moot Court Team and was an Ordered Liberty fellow while studying law. While working as a law clerk for Louisville's Zoppoth Law firm and later for attorney General Daniel Cameron's civil division, he received exposure to several types of civil litigation.

After finishing law school, Mr. Griffee gained vital experience as a prosecutor in Elizabethtown’s Hardin County Attorney's Office, where he presided over both jury and bench trials. He is also a Judge Advocate in the United States Army Reserve, where he serves as an Officer. He can put his legal training to use for his country in this position. Additionally, Mr. Griffee serves in the Kentucky State House of Representatives for both Bullitt and Hardin counties.

Besides spending time with his family, Mr. Griffee enjoys reading, working out and giving back to the community. Call him today if you need legal representation in Bullitt County or the surrounding area.

attorneys.name: H. Philip Grossman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Law Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Philip Grossman has over 35 years of experience in the practice of law and is currently a senior partner in the Louisville Law Firm of Grossman Green PLLC.

His passion is handling personal injury cases for clients who suffer serious and catastrophic injuries. In particular, he most frequently works with victims and families who have suffered the effects of brain injuries, paralysis, fractures, spine injuries and wrongful death.

Recognition And Success

Philip has achieved numerous distinctions. He has been listed in the Kentucky Magazine as a Top Attorney in Kentucky and recognized by Louisville Magazine as a Top Lawyer. From 2007-present, Philip has been selected for inclusion in Kentucky Super Lawyers. Philip is AV Preeminent peer review rated through Martindale-Hubbell.

Philip is also a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum due to his success in obtaining numerous million-dollar verdicts, awards and settlements for his clients.

Community And Law-Related Involvement

In 2018, Philip served as President of the Kentucky Justice Association (KJA) which is the leading organization of Kentucky Plaintiff's Trial Lawyers committed to improving the quality of legal representation for Kentucky injury victims and their families. In 1996 He served as President of the Louisville Bar Association, the largest voluntary bar association for lawyers based in Louisville and Jefferson County, Kentucky.

Philip is also Founder and Master of the Louis D. Brandeis American Inn of Court. He has been a frequent speaker at seminars on medical negligence, spine and brain injury, auto and truck cases and trial practice.

attorneys.name: Richard M Guarnieri
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Frankfort, KY
attorneys.bio:
Richard M. Guarnieri was born in Chicago, Illinois as the second oldest of nine brothers and sisters, three of which have become lawyers as well. When Richard was still a child, his family moved to Frankfort, Kentucky where he was raised and attended Good Shepherd Catholic School and then Franklin County Public Schools until his graduation from Franklin County High School.

Throughout his life, he has attended church with his family at Good Shepherd Catholic Church in Frankfort, Kentucky. In high school, Richard was very active in sports, especially baseball where he continued to play at Centre College. While at Centre College, he was a member of the Beta Theta Pi fraternity and played Varsity Baseball throughout his four years in college.

After graduating from Centre College, Richard enrolled at the University of Kentucky School of Law in 1984. While in law school, he clerked in the summers with Stoll, Keenon & Park at their Frankfort, Kentucky office (now Stoll, Keenon & Ogden, PLLC). After graduating law school in 1986, he joined J. Guthrie True at Stoll, Keenon & Park at their Frankfort, Kentucky office where he began representing clients in personal injury, worker’s compensation, family law, and administrative cases.

Early on in his career, Richard found a passion, and success, in representing clients in personal injury and worker’s compensation cases. Within five years of practicing law, Richard obtained his first $1 million dollar settlement, an achievement that many lawyers never obtain in their entire lives. Since then, Richard has represented hundreds of personal injury and worker’s compensation clients and recovered millions of dollars on their behalf. He has prosecuted personal injury claims against national and international corporations, large trucking companies, international automobile companies, national insurance companies, and other large corporate entities and achieved significant success on behalf of his clients.

In 2012, J. Guthrie True, Richard, and William C. Ayer, Jr. formed True Guarnieri Ayer, LLP. Since that time, Richard has continued to represent clients involving claims of personal injury, worker’s compensation, family law, and civil litigation.

Mr. Guarnieri has been recognized in the areas of workers compensation by the publication The Best Lawyers in America. He is also BV® Distinguished Peer Review Rated by Martindale-Hubbell® for his professionalism and ethics.

attorneys.name: Sarah Hackman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury  Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
While justice is not Sarah's only passion, it is certainly the one that most drives her career. Empathy is her greatest strength. Accountability and compensation are her goals. She will counsel you and fight for you as if you were family.

Prior to attending law school, Sarah was a receptionist and legal assistant at a mid-sized defense firm in Louisville, Kentucky with her eyes set on law school. Unsurprisingly, she quickly realized her dedication was to people rather than corporations and switched sides at the first opportunity.

Sarah has been focused on the Plaintiffs' personal injury work since she obtained her law license in October of 2015. Her experience covers a myriad of fields including product liability, multi-district litigations, nursing home, and elder abuse and neglect, medical malpractice, dram shop, and others. She is a fierce advocate, devoted to exceeding her clients' expectations.

Sarah received her undergraduate degrees in Political Science with an emphasis on Law and Public Policy and Economics at the University of Louisville in 2011, graduating cum laude. She continued her education at U of L's Brandeis School of Law achieving her Juris Doctor in 2015, again graduating cum laude. She was named a Brandeis Scholar and wrote for the Journal of Animal and Environmental Law while completing her studies.

Sarah resides in Louisville, Kentucky with her family, including her three-year-old daughter Arabelle. In her free time, Sarah enjoys gardening, the arts, a good novel or memoir, traveling, and especially volunteering her time for local and national civil rights and justice reform efforts.

attorneys.name: Laura Marie Hagan
attorneys.practice_type: Trademark Law Lawyers in Bowling Green, KY
attorneys.bio:
Laura is a licensed attorney practicing in the South-Central Kentucky region with a concentration in trademark, copyright, and patent law. She advises clients on brand protection and enforcement, conducts clearance searches, and prepares and prosecutes trademark applications. Her experience also includes counseling on copyright registration, licensing, and infringement matters and patent searches, infringement matters and prosecution.

Laura has assisted clients in obtaining U.S. and international trademark and patent rights and routinely provides guidance on related issues such as noncompete agreements and IP-related contracts. She also contributed to the development of Western Kentucky University’s intellectual property policy for its faculty and researchers.

Registered to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, Laura has extensive experience in trademark prosecution, evaluation of products for patent protection, as well as in preparing licenses, agreements, and opinion letters on infringement and validity issues, which allows her to deliver clear, practical advice tailored to her clients' needs.

attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Defense Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Matthew R. Hall joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele in 2016 as an associate in the firm’s Lexington, Kentucky office. Practicing primarily in Workers’ Compensation Defense and Insurance Defense, Matthew is a member of the firm’s Civil Litigation department.

Born April 21, 1986 in Paducah, Kentucky, Matthew moved to Lexington to attend the University of Kentucky where he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Psychology in 2008. He then attended the University of Kentucky College of Law, where he was a member of the Kentucky Law Journal. After graduating from law school in 2012 and passing the Kentucky Bar Exam, Matthew moved to Pikeville, Kentucky, where he practiced with an insurance defense firm that primarily handled medical malpractice cases and served as exclusive counsel for the local regional hospital. In 2014, Matthew joined a solo practitioner’s firm in Pikeville where he worked in numerous fields doing plaintiff’s work, including civil litigation, workers’ compensation, and social security. This work saw him practice throughout eastern Kentucky.

He and his wife Taylor, a registered nurse, live in Nicholasville with their two daughters. He enjoys playing guitar, watching the NFL, NBA, and IndyCar racing, and cheering for the Kentucky wildcats.

attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Henderson, KY
attorneys.bio:
I am proud to call Henderson my home. I graduated from Henderson County High School, where I was a member of the basketball, track, and speech teams, and I'm a member of the Academic Hall of Fame. I then received a scholarship to attend Duke University, before the rivalry with my home state's school began (yes, I have caught much flack since then, but I am a Blue Devil at heart). After finishing law school at the University of Cincinnati, I practiced for a couple of years in Ohio before returning home to raise my four children with my beautiful wife, Emily.

I love helping people, and I love matching wits in court against big-firm and big-company attorneys. I represent people who are hurt - sometimes very badly hurt or killed - through no fault of their own. When I stand before juries and argue cases for my clients, I tell juries that in a court of law, all parties are equal, even if the people on the other side are insurance companies or other big corporations. My team and I provide clients with "big city" legal services, even though we are located in a small town. We fight for our clients in a professional, aggressive, but compassionate manner.

attorneys.name: Sandra B. Hammond
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law, Divorce, Adoption, Custody Disputes Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Hammond is a native of Louisville. She graduated from Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri with majors in Sociology and Spanish. She spent her junior year abroad in Madrid, Spain. Ms. Hammond received a Master of Arts in Foreign Language Education in 1979 from the University of Louisville prior to graduating from law school. She has extensive experience representing clients in Family Law matters including child custody disputes, juvenile court matters, divorce litigation, adoptions and co-parenting matters. She has served as a Guardian Ad Litem in Jefferson Family Court for twenty years, representing child who have been abused and neglected

Ms. Hammond is a certified Family Court Mediator where she mediates all types of family court issues and disputes.

In addition, she is a court-approved Parent Coordinator who is appointed in high-conflict divorce cases to address parenting concerns such as timesharing, education for the children, participation in extracurricular activities and creating co-parenting tools.

Ms. Hammond is also an influential civic leader. She has been a Trustee of the Board of Directors of Key One Healthcare and Jewish Hospital and St. Mary’s Healthcare. She has served as past chair of the Board of Trustees of the Jewish Heritage Fund for Excellence, a Kentucky Foundation with $250,000,000.00 of assets.

In addition to her Family Law focus, Ms. Hammond's practice includes estate planning and probate matters.

Ms. Hammond is married, has two adult children and two grandchildren.

John E. Hanley is a native of Louisville, Kentucky. He attended Saint Xavier High School and obtained his undergraduate and law degrees from nationally ranked Georgetown University, located in Washington, D.C. After graduating from law school, he began his career with the regional law firm, Greenebaum Doll & McDonald, PLLC.

In 1997, Mr. Hanley teamed with Michael A. Valenti to form the law firm now known as Valenti Hanley PLLC.

Mr. Hanley primarily serves as outside general counsel for a number of businesses located in Kentucky and advises them on a host of legal issues. Mr. Hanley devotes the rest of his practice to civil litigation for both the plaintiff and defendant with an emphasis on general business litigation & employment litigation.

During the course of his career, Mr. Hanley has obtained significant experience in both State and Federal Courts and has litigated hundreds of cases.

In litigating matters, Mr. Hanley’s first goal for any client is aggressive representation but with an eye on the economics at stake in the matter. Mr. Hanley strives to achieve quick, economic, and satisfactory resolution to any dispute before engaging in full blown litigation. If a matter is not able to be resolved at the outset, he stands ready to litigate a matter to judgment.

Mr. Hanley is also active in the community having served on the board of directors of the following organizations: the Kentucky Derby Museum, the Beacon House, Big Spring Country Club, Actors Theatre of Louisville, and the Louisville Bar Association. Mr. Hanley is also a member of Holy Trinity parish where he has coached girls basketball for many years.

Mr. Hanley primarily serves as outside general counsel for a number of businesses located in Kentucky and advises them on a host of legal issues. Mr. Hanley devotes the rest of his practice to civil litigation for both the plaintiff and defendant with an emphasis on general business litigation & employment litigation.

During the course of his career, Mr. Hanley has obtained significant experience in both State and Federal Courts and has litigated hundreds of cases.

In litigating matters, Mr. Hanley’s first goal for any client is aggressive representation but with an eye on the economics at stake in the matter. Mr. Hanley strives to achieve quick, economic, and satisfactory resolution to any dispute before engaging in full blown litigation. If a matter is not able to be resolved at the outset, he stands ready to litigate a matter to judgment.

Mr. Hanley is also active in the community having served on the board of directors of the following organizations: the Kentucky Derby Museum, the Beacon House, Big Spring Country Club, Actors Theatre of Louisville, and the Louisville Bar Association. Mr. Hanley is also a member of Holy Trinity parish where he has coached girls basketball for many years.

attorneys.bio:
Aaron Harper has been with Edwards and Kautz since 2014. Before that, he was a law clerk, a litigation associate, a financial advisor and an Assistant Public Advocate for the Department of Public Advocacy’s Paducah Trial Office.

Aaron became an attorney because the law “touches everything”. This means it is linked to many different professions and fields. He wants to help people who are unable to help themselves. He joined the firm because of the way the firm stands for its clients and the firm believes in helping its clients solve their unique problems.

Aaron focuses his practice on personal injury and car accidents, including Workers’ Compensation and Social Security Disability. He avidly helps those who have been injured by the negligent, careless actions of others. And he is fervent about protecting the interests of those accused of crimes.

He was admitted to practice before the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit; the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit; and the United States District Courts for the Western and Eastern Districts of Kentucky.

attorneys.practice_type: Car Wrecks, Truck Wrecks, ATV Accidents, Boat Accidents, Defective Products, Motorcycle Wrecks, Truc Lawyers in Somerset, KY
attorneys.bio:
Rhonda Hatfield-Jeffers obtained her BA from The University of Kentucky in 1995 and obtained her Juris Doctor from Louis D. Brandeis School of Law, University of Louisville, in 1999. She was admitted to the practice of law in Kentucky in 1999, admitted to the U.S. District Court Eastern District of Kentucky in 2001, the U.S. District Court Western District of Kentucky in 2001 and the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in 2023.

Her entire career has been focused on advocating for those who have been injured by the negligence of others. She has represented individuals injured in car wrecks, truck wrecks, motorcycle wrecks, boating accidents, product liability cases, medical malpractice and other accidents and/or injuries caused by the carelessness of others for over 23 years. Rhonda served as a member of the Kentucky Justice Association's Executive Committee from 2018-2022. She was President of the Kentucky Justice Association in 2021 and continues to serve on the Board of Governors as a Past President.

Rhonda served on the Kentucky Bar Associations' Attorney Advertising Committee from 2014-2019. She has served as a member of the Kentucky Character and Fitness Committee from 2021 to the present. Rhonda was named a member of the National Trial Lawyers Top 100- Civil Plaintiff in 2019 and continues to be a member. She is a Life Member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum. Rhonda is a Life Fellow of the Kentucky Bar Foundation. She is one of the select attorneys listed in The Million Dollar Verdicts Section of the Kentucky Trial Court Review as having more than one-million-dollar verdict.

attorneys.name: Allison M. Helsinger
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Defense Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Allison Helsinger joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele in 2014 and currently serves as a partner in the firm’s Lexington, Kentucky office. Practicing primarily in Workers’ Compensation and Insurance Defense, Helsinger is a member of the firm’s Civil Litigation department. She is a top-rated attorney providing legal representation in Kentucky for a variety of different issues. Helsinger was selected to Rising Stars for 2019 through 2021 and recognized as a Top Leader in the Law for 2024 by Women We Admire.

Originally from West Chester, Ohio, a suburb just north of Cincinnati, Helsinger first moved to Kentucky to attend Eastern Kentucky University, where she graduated with her Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science in 2007. Upon graduation, she moved to Lexington, Kentucky, to attend the University of Kentucky College of Law. During her time in law school, Helsinger was active with the Trial Advocacy Board, the Student Bar Association, and the College’s renowned, Legal Clinic, providing legal services to low-income persons in Lexington and its surrounding areas. After graduating in 2010 and successfully passing the Kentucky Bar Exam, she joined a regional civil defense firm as an associate in their Lexington office, where she practiced motor vehicle liability, premises liability, product liability, and some employment law throughout the Commonwealth. Currently, her primary practice is in workers’ compensation defense, but the office also specializes in civil subrogation, business and transactional matters, civil liability, and collections.

Helsinger is admitted to practice in Kentucky and permitted to appear before the Eastern and Western, United States District Courts, as well as the Supreme Court of Kentucky. She is a member of the Fayette County Bar Association, the Kentucky Bar Association, the Kentucky Defense Counsel, the Women’s Law Association, and the Central Kentucky American Inns of Court. She lives in Lexington, Kentucky, where she is actively involved with the Ronald McDonald House Charities of the Bluegrass, the Eastern Kentucky University Alumni Board, and the Chi Omega Fraternity. Specifically, Helsinger is a volunteer member of Chi Omega’s legal education team, traveling to college campuses and providing legal education on hot-button issues relevant to women attending college in today’s legal climate.

attorneys.name: Paul J. Hershberg
attorneys.practice_type: General Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
For more than two decades, Paul has represented individuals and small businesses in state and federal courts in a wide range of commercial disputes, simple and complex. Within the realm of general commercial litigation, Paul has extensive experience litigating insurance coverage disputes, including extra-contractual claims, partnership and corporate separations and related claims, construction disputes, and matters of governmental and sovereign immunity. In addition to maintaining an active litigation practice, Paul is regularly retained by other attorneys to assist or lead in appellate cases, from briefing through oral arguments. Paul also provides litigation management in complex matters, including consultation and guidance regarding the storage, preservation, and production of electronically stored information.

At both the trial and appellate levels, Paul is regarded by his peers and the bench as thorough, detail-oriented, prepared, diligent, and fair. Paul has attained the AV Preeminent rating from Martindale-Hubbell, been recognized as a Top Lawyer in Louisville on several occasions by Louisville Magazine, and has been selected a Kentucky Super Lawyer in every year since 2010. (Despite the name, this distinction has not positively affected Paul's height, looks, or athletic ability.)

When not working, Paul enjoys acquiring jazz records.

attorneys.name: Joshua Daniel Hicks
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Josh went to middle school and high school in Fleming County, where he lived on a farm with this family. His father, Dan, worked construction and his mother, Sharon, worked at the local Honda shop. Josh spent his high school years working on various farms (including the family farm) pitching hay, housing tobacco, and building fence.

Josh was a standout offensive and defensive lineman at Fleming County High School and went to Georgetown College to continue his football and academic career. After three semesters, he left college to work for the same construction company as his father. After a year or so as an iron worker and rigger, he joined the United States Marine Corps where he was trained as a radio operator and cryptographic custodian. He married his wife, Bethany, who was born and raised in Maysville, Kentucky, during the first year of his service. Josh served aboard the USS Ponce and the USS Trenton during two deployments with the 24th Marine Expeditionary Unit. He received his honorable discharge after four years of service, just after the birth of his and Bethany’s beautiful daughter, Kaitlin.

After his Marine Corps service ended, Josh completed training as a certified police officer at EKU’s Department of Criminal Justice Training and began working as a police officer in Bethany’s hometown. Josh spent five years as a Maysville Police Officer, serving on the Emergency Response Team and as a certified training officer, training new police recruits. Three years in, Bethany and Josh celebrated the birth of their son, Daniel. Because he worked nights and weekends at the police department, Josh was able to go back to school at Morehead State University during the day and graduated with honors. During his time at Morehead State, he began to consider a career as an attorney.

After graduation from Morehead State, Josh applied to and was accepted into the University of Kentucky College of Law. He was a competitor on national trial teams all three years of law school and built strong ties to the city of Lexington, where his wife opened an insurance agency and his children began attending school. After law school, Josh went to work for a mid-size firm in Lexington where he litigated and practiced cases from Paducah to Pikeville. He moved to a regional firm’s Lexington office where he continued to practice with and be mentored by some of the most respected attorneys in the state of Kentucky. He has represented individuals and businesses across the state in a wide variety of matters, conducting and participating in hundreds of depositions, oral arguments, mediations, and several jury trials. Josh volunteers his time as a mediator for the Fayette District Court.

attorneys.name: Jesse R. Hodgson
attorneys.practice_type: Banking and Finance Law, Foreclosure and Loan Workouts, Uniform Commercial Code Lawyers in Mount Sterling, KY
attorneys.bio:
Jesse R. Hodgson utilizes the ability to “think outside the box” as well as use of conventional methods to assist clients to arrive at their desired destination. He helps clients determine their objectives and goals from the beginning and helps clients meet these objectives so as to ensure maximum value to the client.

Jesse handles complex loan transactions, workouts, modifications and restructuring of debt. He provides a variety of legal services and counsel for financial institutions ensuring compliance with federal and state banking regulations.

Additionally, Jesse handles the collection of past due debts for a wide variety of industries and individuals and also represents consumers to settle past due debts.

Jesse provides counsel for corporate structuring. He is able to provide advice and assist clients in the formation, dissolution, purchase and/or sale of businesses, including stock purchases/sales and asset purchases/sales. His expertise in business formation ensures compliance with state and federal regulations for diverse and numerous industries.

He is also able to assist existing business in governance, employment agreements and non-compete agreements. Jesse provides contract formation and documentation, contract review, negotiation of existing of proposed contracts and dispute resolution of contractual terms.

In the area of real estate law, Jesse provides counsel for real estate purchases and sales, including land contracts, mortgages, promissory notes, leases, subdivision, condominiums and real property financing, whether individual or corporate. Jesse performs numerous real estate closings each year, which includes providing title examinations, title opinions, title insurance policies and drafting closing documentation.

Jesse also has considerable experience with estate planning and estate administration. He uses numerous devices of estate planning and existing law to effectively ensure the proper and efficient transfer of wealth from generation to generation, no matter the size of the estate. Jesse is able to advise and reduce the possible implications of estate tax through proper planning so as to achieve the desired results of his clients. In the area of estate planning, Jesse provides a variety of documentation, including wills, revocable trusts, irrevocable trusts, powers of attorney, health care powers of attorney and living wills.

Jesse also handles numerous probate estates to assist heirs in the administration of the estate and proper distribution of assets and payment of claims. This includes the appointment of executors, administrators and trustees in the probate process as well as the preparation of state and federal estate tax returns and inheritance tax returns.

Jesse provides counsel in the area of elder law, particularly Medicaid planning, to ensure compliance with existing law and provide advice to those seeking Medicaid eligibility. Jesse is able to counsel those seeking Medicaid eligibility, and their loved ones, about the qualification process and how to effectively obtain and retain Medicaid qualification.

Jesse also provides numerous services in the area of construction law. He has worked with contractors to provide contract review, negotiation, dispute resolution, collections, lien preparation and lien enforcement regarding both private construction jobs and high profile state jobs, including highway construction and building construction.

Jesse is a lifelong resident of Mount Sterling, Kentucky and much of his family resides in the area.

In his free time, Jesse enjoys horse racing, golfing, traveling, tennis and volunteering his time to serve others in numerous civic and charitable activities.

attorneys.name: William L. Hoge III
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Bill Hoge was admitted to the Kentucky Bar Association in 1972. He has four decades of civil litigation and complex domestic relations case experience in Louisville, Kentucky. William L. Hoge, III is a trained divorce and Family Law mediator and a Collaborative Divorce and Family Law practitioner.

A Fellow in the prestigious American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, he is the former President of the Kentucky Chapter of the AAML as well as the former Chair of the Family Law Sections for both the Kentucky Bar Association and the Louisville Bar Association.

Memberships:

Kentucky Collaborative Family Law Network, Inc.

Family Law Solutions, PLLC

Kentucky Bar Association

Attorney William L. Hoge's practice concentrates almost exclusively in Family Law with particular emphasis in complex divorce actions.

Mr. Hoge received a Bachelor of Science degree in Commerce from the University of Louisville in 1969, where he also attended Law School and from which he received his Juris Doctorate in 1972. Mr. Hoge attended the Hastings College of Law, College of Trial Advocacy in 1975; the University of Kentucky College of Trial Advocacy in 1986.

Mr. Hoge has extensive experience as a presenter as many Continuing Legal Education events on the subjects of Family Law, Domestic Violence, Collaborative Law, Ethics, Psychology, Trial Technique, Demonstrative Evidence and Mediation Training.

In addition to his membership and participation in the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, the Kentucky Bar Association and the Louisville Bar Association, he is a member of the KBA Lawyers Helping Lawyers Committee and the KBA Child Protection & Domestic Violence Committee. Mr. Hoge is a former member and founding member of the American Bar Association's Commission on Lawyer Assistance Programs and a member of the ABA Family Law Section.

Mr. Hoge is a past member of the Jefferson County Family Court's Family Support Center Advisory Committee, the Family Court Advisory Committee (Divorce Rules Committee Chair) and the Family Court Mediator Review Committee.

Mr. Hoge is also a member of the Kentucky Justice Association.

Mr. Hoge was honored by the Louisville Bar Association as the recipient of the 1999 Judge Richard A. Revell Family Law Practitioner of the Year Award.

Mr. Hoge is the co-author and publisher of Divorce in Kentucky The Dissolution Resolution System, an Interactive Organizer and Video, 1997 and has extensive experience as a CLE and motivational speaker before the ABA, AAML, KBA and LBA.

Mr. Hoge was the Assistant Jefferson County Attorney (1972-1976); the Chief Prosecutor for Jefferson County Attorney (1976-1982); the General Counsel to International Union of Electrical Workers, Local 761 at General Electric (1975-1988); the General Counsel to Kentucky State District Council of Carpenters, AFL-CIO (UBCJA) (1988-1991) and has been in General Private Legal Practice since 1972.

In addition to his many years of practice before the Jefferson County Circuit, Family and District Courts in Louisville, Mr. Hoge is admitted to and has practiced before the Kentucky Supreme Court (since 1972); the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals (since 1974); the U.S. District Court, Western District of Kentucky (since 1973); the U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Kentucky (since 1975), and the U.S. Supreme Court (since 1975).

attorneys.name: Travis L. Holtrey
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Owensboro, KY
attorneys.bio:
My family instilled in me a strong work ethic and a dedication to perform beyond expectations, no matter what the task. Beginning at age ten, I spent my summers working on my grandparent’s farm in Ohio. When most kids were spending summertime enjoying vacations and a break from school, I was working on a dairy farm sixty to seventy hours a week. I learned the importance of hard work and the value of money. I saw my Grandmother work four jobs to keep the farm running after my Grandfather passed away. I dedicated my time in school to academic excellence and upon graduating high school I knew I wanted to be an attorney. I received a scholarship for academic debate while attending Western Kentucky University. As the captain of the debate team I led the team from a national ranking of #165 to #4 in only two years. In Law School, I competed in moot court and national negotiation competitions where again we achieved national recognition, placing eighth in the nation in moot court competition.

I take what I learned from my childhood and early teen years and now use the same dedication to the work I perform for my clients. Since 1995, I have assisted people across the state of Kentucky and throughout the United States who have been injured and need guidance because of a variety of unfortunate circumstances. I have had the privilege to represent individuals and families, injured or killed due to dangerous products such as farm implements, coal mining machinery, elevators and firearms. I have litigated medical malpractice cases involving dental extractions, gallbladder removal, diabetic management, orthopedic surgery and emergency treatment and diagnosis of post-surgical complications. I have represented clients suffering from chemical exposures including anhydrous ammonia and coal dust. I have concluded cases involving pharmaceutical mistakes involving errors with prescription medications, infusions, vaccination injury and intravenous administration. Finally, I have tried, mediated and settled hundreds of cases resulting from trucking wrecks, bus wrecks and car wrecks.

In 2018, I began shifting much of my practice to business litigation. I found the challenges of representing businesses in disputes tested my skills as an attorney. I have represented numerous regional businesses in complex contract disputes, shareholder disputes, and transactional issues. I experienced first hand how litigating business cases transfers many skills necessary for litigating all types of cases and truly makes an attorney well rounded for any adversarial matter.

In my personal time, I have competed and finished two full length Ironman competitions. I have taught myself how to play the guitar. I have learned how to perform many home renovation projects and most importantly, I have raised four unbelievable daughters and three super stepsons.

The list below contains some of my career highlights. I look forward to being an advocate for many more people and businesses as we move ahead making a difference one case at a time.

attorneys.name: John Hopper
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fort Mitchell, KY
attorneys.bio:
I wasn’t born into the legal profession. Growing up, the thought of becoming a lawyer never crossed my mind. My legal journey began on the same dirt road as many of you that are reading this is on … as a client. I had a child very young and sought legal advice about my visitation rights. I met with an attorney that advised me that it would be cheaper to sign my rights away and then just find him when he turned 18. I was flabbergasted at that notion! The problem was that he didn’t see me as a person, I was just another file on his desk. I have never forgotten that feeling of despair and lost while hearing that, I promise that no client… no person will ever feel that while sitting across from my desk.

Years of being in and out of family court I would observe countless individuals speaking with their attorneys. There were a lot of good attorneys who cared about their clients, however there were far too many that didn’t. That’s what spurred me to become an attorney. I have a blue-collar background, born and raised in NKY and come from a hard-working family. I was in fact the first person in my family to receive their doctorate degree. I know what it's like to work hard and come up short and the struggle to put food on the table. My years of non-profit management working with both the elderly and individuals with disabilities also instilled a level of personal care that I invoke with all my clients.

When you read one attorney bio, you have read them all. It’s the usual “look at me” approach. A cold and clinical synopsis of all their achievement and associations. I threw a few of those below in case you were interest, but let’s face it, you’re probably not. Most clients can’t relate to that information. And really, this shouldn’t be about the attorney. This isn’t my story, this is your story.

I have served as a head football coach and baseball coach in northern Kentucky for over a decade. I’m a diehard Cincinnati Reds and Bengals fan. I promise if you’re a Steelers fan not to hold it against you. I enjoy amusement parks and water parks. You could even call me a bit of a Disney fanatic! I’m also a former foster care parent that adopted his children. Like I said, my story reads as many of your stories do.

The ugly truth is with some lawyers, they are watching the seconds tick by while they are meeting with you. To them, every minute represents potential fees. With myself, I believe I have a higher duty than just giving you legal advice. I’m there to listen to your pain, your fears and concerns. In short, I am there FOR YOU and to relentlessly pursue your rights. Your more than just a file and my promise to you is I will treat you like the person you deserve to be treated as.

attorneys.bio:
Nanci, a southeastern Kentucky native, is a partner at White, McCann & Stewart, PLLC and practices mainly in the area of family law and contract formation and dispute. Nanci appears regularly in Clark, Madison, Fayette, Powell and Montgomery Circuit and Family courts, as well as several of the other surrounding counties.

Nanci graduated magna cum laude from Transylvania University in 2000, with a B.A. in History and a minor in Political Science. While at Transylvania, Nanci was the Chief Hearing Officer for the Student Judicial Board, was a member of the Omicron Delta Kappa leadership honorary, was Phi Alpha Theta history honorary president, was on the dance team, was a Student Orientation Leader, was a writing center tutor and was involved in many other service and community organizations. Nanci graduated cum laude from the University of Kentucky College of Law in 2003, where she was in the top 11% of her class and received the CALI award in Torts. While at UK law school, Nanci was an editor for the Kentucky Law Journal, was a member of the Honor Council, was a member of the Trial Advocacy Board, was President of the Women's Law Caucus and was historian for the Phi Delta Phi legal fraternity.

Nanci was sworn in as a member of the Kentucky Bar Association in 2003 and has practiced at White, McCann & Stewart, PLLC since that time. Nanci is also licensed to practice law in federal court, in the Eastern District of Kentucky and before the United States Supreme Court. Nanci became a partner at White, McCann & Stewart, PLLC in 2008. Nanci is a member of the Clark, Madison and Fayette county bar associations.

Nanci is an active member of many community and service organizations. In 2013, Nanci received the Kentucky Bar Association's Young Lawyers' Service to the Community Award. Nanci is a Past President of the Junior League of Lexington and has served on numerous boards and committees. Nanci won the 2016 Junior League of Lexington Volunteer of the Year award. Nanci serves on the board of directors for the Chrysalis House and has served as President. Nanci is on the board of directors for The Well and is otherwise very involved in attempting to better her community.

Nanci's practice is varied and includes all areas of family law, including but not limited to divorce, custody, paternity, child support, timesharing, grandparents' rights, pre-nuptial agreement, post-nuptial agreements, termination of parental rights and abuse, neglect and dependency. Nanci has also worked extensively as Guardian Ad Litem for children. Nanci also handles contract formation and dispute, general civil litigation, appellate practice, estate planning, social security disability (SSI and RSDI), personal injury, administrative law and appeals, business entity formation, collection, and medical malpractice.

Nanci appears regularly in Clark, Madison, Fayette, Powell and Montgomery Circuit and Family courts, as well as several of the other surrounding counties.

Nanci graduated magna cum laude from Transylvania University in 2000, with a B.A. in History and a minor in Political Science. While at Transylvania, Nanci was the Chief Hearing Officer for the Student Judicial Board, was a member of the Omicron Delta Kappa leadership honorary, was Phi Alpha Theta history honorary president, was on the dance team, was a Student Orientation Leader, was a writing center tutor and was involved in many other service and community organizations. Nanci graduated cum laude from the University of Kentucky College of Law in 2003, where she was in the top 11% of her class and received the CALI award in Torts. While at UK law school, Nanci was an editor for the Kentucky Law Journal, was a member of the Honor Council, was a member of the Trial Advocacy Board, was President of the Women's Law Caucus and was historian for the Phi Delta Phi legal fraternity.

Nanci was sworn in as a member of the Kentucky Bar Association in 2003 and has practiced at White, McCann & Stewart, PLLC since that time. Nanci is also licensed to practice law in federal court, in the Eastern District of Kentucky and before the United States Supreme Court. Nanci became a partner at White, McCann & Stewart, PLLC in 2008. Nanci is a member of the Clark, Madison and Fayette county bar associations.

Nanci is an active member of many community and service organizations. In 2013, Nanci received the Kentucky Bar Association's Young Lawyers' Service to the Community Award. Nanci is a Past President of the Junior League of Lexington and has served on numerous boards and committees. Nanci won the 2016 Junior League of Lexington Volunteer of the Year award. Nanci serves on the board of directors for the Chrysalis House and has served as President. Nanci is on the board of directors for The Well and is otherwise very involved in attempting to better her community.

Nanci's practice is varied and includes all areas of family law, including but not limited to divorce, custody, paternity, child support, timesharing, grandparents' rights, pre-nuptial agreement, post-nuptial agreements, termination of parental rights and abuse, neglect and dependency. Nanci has also worked extensively as Guardian Ad Litem for children. Nanci also handles contract formation and dispute, general civil litigation, appellate practice, estate planning, social security disability (SSI and RSDI), personal injury, administrative law and appeals, business entity formation, collection, and medical malpractice.
