attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Heather Humble is a native of Lexington, Kentucky, where she attended the University of Kentucky. Driven by her long-standing goal of becoming an attorney, she went on to attend the University of Dayton School of Law.

Following law school, Heather began her legal career with the Department of Public Advocacy before joining the Commonwealth Attorney’s Office in 2016. Over the next eight years, she served as a prosecutor in the 16th, 30th, and 53th Judicial Circuits. During her tenure, she gained extensive trial experience handling a broad range of cases, including general criminal prosecutions, white-collar crime, narcotics, robbery, burglary, violent assaults, domestic violence, murder, and sexually based offenses.

Continuing her commitment to public service, Heather later accepted a position with the Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services, where she worked to protect children from abuse and neglect.

In 2025, Heather joined Sewell & Neal, bringing with her a wealth of courtroom experience, a passion for advocacy, and a strong dedication to achieving results for her clients.

In her free time, Heather loves traveling, spending time with her loved ones, and relaxing with her little dog, Henry.

attorneys.name: Kenneth C. Human
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Kenny Human’s eventual route to a law career began in dramatic fashion. A native of New Orleans, Kenny departed the city to begin his undergraduate career at the University of Michigan just two days before the city’s levees broke as a result of Hurricane Katrina. In fact, his plane was the last to leave New Orleans before the storm arrived. Though his family’s home was flooded and sadly lost to the devastating storm, Kenny persevered despite this adversity. According to Kenny, “Enduring the loss of my family home and witnessing the horrible things people in my city endured helped prepare me for helping others in some of the most difficult times in their lives.”

He later secured a Bachelor of Arts degree in The Political Economy of Crime with a minor in Spanish from the University of Michigan in 2009. In fact, Kenny petitioned the university to create this major with the support of noted criminologists Charles Bright and P.J. McGann, Ph.D. “This is an interdisciplinary major allowing students to explore all the forces contributing to the ebb-and-flow of crime in our society – I am very proud to have played a role in establishing this area of study at my alma mater.”

While an undergraduate, Kenny worked for the United States Marshal Service and Joint Terrorism Task Force in Houston, the Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms & Explosives in the ATF field office in Washington, DC, and as a creative writing professor at the Parr Correctional Facility in Adrian, Michigan. Kenny still serves on the University of Michigan’s College of Literature, Science & Art’s Scholarship Advisory Committee.

While completing law school, he worked in the Harris County, Texas District Attorney’s Office, as well as for H. Wayne Roberts’ criminal defense practice.

Kenny is also past president of the Kentucky Criminal Law Society, an organization he founded for law students, past vice president of the National Latino/Latina Law Student Association, and was a member of UK Law’s Tournament of Champions Trial Litigation Team that competed around the county in Mock Trial competitions.

Immediately after completing law school, Kenny worked for a large insurance defense firm until March of 2014. During his time there he represented businesses and individuals in cases involving automobile accidents, slip-and-fall cases, construction defects, medical malpractice, insurance company bad faith, and other personal injury cases. Kenny then transitioned to a large Plaintiff's practice where he was able to utilize his keen understanding of defense practices intended to minimize the claims of personal injury litigants.

Now, after having served countless Kentuckians on both sides of the aisle in over 50 Kentucky counties, Kenny has come to our firm being able to bring a more personal approach to his practice. For Kenny, a more personal approach will mean devoting himself to the individual needs of his clients and applying his extensive experience to the subtle legal issues involved in their case.

In his off-time, Kenny enjoys cheering for his beloved New Orleans Saints, spoiling his two shelter rescues, Marques and Colston, and advancing his Judo practice (he has an Orange Belt).

Awards and Honors

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Covington, KY
attorneys.bio:
My name is Joseph Ireland. I am one of the firm's managing partners. Since my first year of law school, I knew I wanted to be a trial attorney. I am proud to say I followed my passion and have never given up my drive to become one of the best attorneys in my field.

On my journey, I have been fortunate to gain more courtroom experience than most will ever see. I started off working in a high-volume plaintiff's personal injury firm, it was baptism by fire. Eventually, my career took me to a firm that specialized in complex litigation all across the country. Many of the cases I worked had catastrophic damages and involved cutting edge legal issues against the best litigators in the country.

In 2010, I decided it was time to open my own firm and begin building my own local practice. That decision has been deeply rewarding and provided me the opportunity to represent more than 1,000 minors and their families. Today, Russell & Ireland Law Group, LLC has grown into a highly successful litigation firm that is proud of the way it helps its clients and community.

When I am not representing clients, I enjoy hiking, camping, and soccer. I volunteer as a soccer coach for the YMCA and can never say no to a home improvement project.

attorneys.name: Erin C. S. Izzo
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Frankfort, KY
attorneys.bio:
A Kentucky native, Erin C. S. Izzo has served as a litigator across the Commonwealth for more than 20 years. She has represented clients from trial through appeal in state and federal courts, and state agencies in matters concerning personal injury, professional malpractice, employment litigation, and workers’ compensation, among other areas. Erin has presented many seminars to attorneys, paralegals, and Human Resources representatives on employment law matters, such as the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Civil Rights Act, the Pregnancy Discrimination Act, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, and the Kentucky Workers’ Compensation Act.

Erin is well-known for her expertise as an Arbitrator, having served as a neutral in matters involving complex injuries, medical malpractice, nursing home/hospital malpractice, employment disputes, and contractual disputes. Outside of arbitration, Erin has also served as a Mediator in numerous types of cases, including but not limited to mass tort, personal injury, coal mining, premises liability, contracts, and wrongful death, to name a few.

In her free time, Erin volunteers by working with students at the high school, college, and law school levels on mock trial competitions. As a classically trained violinist, Erin has had the privilege to rock on stage several times with the band Disturbed in their cover of Simon and Garfunkel’s Sound of Silence.

attorneys.bio:
Clark Johnson’s practice focuses on complex business disputes and class action litigation. Mr. Johnson represents business entities, directors, officers and shareholders in a wide range of litigation. He has litigated and tried corporate governance and control matters, lender liability claims, shareholder disputes and derivative actions, restrictive covenant suits, securities and consumer fraud cases, construction matters and franchise disputes, among others. He has litigated cases in twenty-three states.

Examples of Mr. Johnson’s class action work include defending life insurance companies in cost of insurance increase and failure to decrease cases, vanishing premium cases, modal premium cases, DAC tax cases, effective-date cases and interest crediting cases. He has extensive experience in class litigation concerning fixed index annuities and universal life insurance. In addition, Mr. Johnson has litigated FLSA collective actions involving several difference industries, ERISA class actions, and state consumer protection act and California UCL and elder abuse matters. Mr. Johnson also has defended class actions against mortgage companies involving payoff statement fees and predatory lending, and TILA claims against credit card issues.

Examples of Mr. Johnson’s experience in securities-related litigation include the defense of a number of securities fraud class actions and shareholder suits, and prosecution and defense of FINRA arbitrations. In addition, Mr. Johnson has significant experience in representing issuers, officers and others in SEC investigations and enforcement actions, and in internal corporate investigations.

Mr. Johnson represents clients across a variety of industries including financial services and banking, construction, transportation, real estate development, food and beverage, hospitality, and manufacturing.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Johnson was a partner at a large regional firm for thirteen years. He also was an associate (1996-2001) and then an equity partner (2002-2004) at Jenner & Block LLP in Chicago. Mr. Johnson began his legal career as a law clerk to the Honorable S. content: PHT Holding I, LLC v. Sec. Life of Denver Ins. Co., No. 23-1326, 2024 WL 4765530 (10th Cir. Nov. 13, 2024). Mr. Johnson served as lead trial counsel for Security Life of Denver at the district court and argued the appeal in this cost-of-insurance class action. The Tenth Circuit affirmed the district court’s summary judgment ruling in favor of Security Life of Denver.

SuperAsh Remainderman, LP v. Ashland, LLC, --- S.W.3d ---, No. 2023-CA-0427-DG, 2024 WL 4521291 (Ky. Ct. App. Oct. 18, 2024). Mr. Johnson represented a commercial landlord in a series of forcible detainer cases and successfully argued at the Court of Appeals, obtaining a reversal of the lower courts’ refusal to issue eviction orders.

Ooten v. Hillcrest Nursing Home of Corbin, Inc., No. 6:23-CV-202-REW-HAI, 2024 WL 4045444 (E.D. Ky. Sept. 4, 2024). Mr. Johnson represented a skilled nursing facility and related defendants in a series of class actions alleging that the facilities were understaffed. The district courts granted defendants’ motions to dismiss for failure to state a claim.

ISCO Industries v. O’Neill, No. 2020-ci-3079 (Jefferson Cir. Ct., Ky). Mr. Johnson served as lead trial counsel for defendant in this restrictive covenants case. After a number of claims were dismissed, the matter was tried to a jury for a week in March 2024. The jury return a verdict completely in favor of defendant.

Holbert v. Vittitow Refrigeration, Inc., No. 3:20-CV-114-DJH-CHL, 2023 WL 12004725 (W.D. Ky. Mar. 31, 2023). Mr. Johnson served as lead trial counsel for plan trustees in this ERISA action concerning interim valuation of plan assets. After a bench trial, the court declined to award plaintiff any recovery.

Edwards Moving & Rigging, Inc. v. Sims Crane, Inc., 2020 WL 7707025 (M.D. Fla. Dec. 29, 2020). Mr. Johnson served as lead trial counsel for plaintiff in this contract and business tort action in federal court in Tampa. The court entered a partial preliminary injunction, and then plaintiff established that defendants were in contempt of the injunction. After a three-day bench trial in Summer 2020, the Court entered a permanent injunction in favor of plaintiff.

Abbit v. ING USA Annuity & Life Ins. Co., 774 Fed. Appx. 351 (9th Cir. 2019). Mr. Johnson served as lead trial counsel for defendant in this class action relating to fixed indexed annuities. The district court granted defendant’s motion for summary judgment and the Ninth Circuit affirmed.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiffs Lawyers in Pikeville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Gary C. Johnson has been representing Plaintiffs in personal injury cases for over 40 years. He is the founder of Gary C. Johnson, P.S.C. which currently has 13 attorneys in four offices located in Pikeville, Lexington, Louisville and Hazard, Kentucky.

Gary C. Johnson and his firm are listed in the Martindale Hubbell Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers and he has been named a Kentucky Super Lawyer for the last two years. In 2008, Gary C. Johnson was awarded the Peter Perlman Outstanding Trial Lawyer of the Year Award by the Kentucky Justice Association for his work as an advocate for the rights of the people and his service as a mentor to young lawyers in the state.

He has received several multi-million dollar jury verdicts and settlements over his long and distinguished career. He has the largest personal injury jury verdict of any lawyer in the state of Kentucky. He has tried cases in Kentucky, Georgia and West Virginia. He has also handled cases in several other states.

Gary C. Johnson continues to devote the majority of his time to the day-to-day practice of law. His firm's practice consists entirely of Plaintiff personal injury cases in the fields of vehicular negligence, products liability, and medical malpractice. In the last few years, however, Gary has diverted some of his time to the education of other trial lawyers. He has presented seminars for the Kentucky Bar Association, Kentucky Justice Association and the American Association of Justice on trial strategy and how to maximize damages in your case.

Over a period of four years Gary was involved in national research of juror attitudes. Gary C. Johnson, David Ball, Don Keenan, and Jim Fitzgerald set out to determine if there was a way to counter the insurance companies' propaganda which had literally poisoned modern jurors against injured victims. After four years of focus groups across the country the group concluded that there was an answer. A decision was made to share the research with other plaintiff lawyers and this led to the publication of the book, "Reptile - The 2009 Manual of the Plaintiff's Revolution". David Ball and Don Keenan, two members of the research group are the authors of this book. This research "wrote the book" for the modern approach to jury persuasion.

Gary C. Johnson has over the years helped new lawyers on an individual basis represent injured people. He is pleased that many of his proven methods have been published. He is sharing with the Plaintiff's Bar the secrets of his success as a preeminent trial lawyer. Gary recently authored a chapter on Judo Law in "Reptile in the Mist" by David Ball and Don Keenan

attorneys.bio:
Jim grew up in Annandale, Virginia the eldest of four children. Jim's parents grew up in southern West Virginia and had moved to the DC metro area in the early 1960s for work and educational opportunities. During high school Jim excelled at small-bore rifle marksmanship, being the Virginia state prone champion for three years and was recognized as the Most Valuable Player on his high school football team as a senior.

Jim attended West Virginia University where he and several other students re-colonized the Tau Kappa Epsilon Fraternity. Jim served two years as chaplain and one year as president. Jim graduated in 1987 with a Bachelor of Arts in psychology.

Following two years of study at Emory University Chandler School of Theology Jim worked in the Atlanta, Georgia landscape industry and at Home Depot.

Jim married his former wife Lynne in 1989 in Dalton, Georgia and returned to West Virginia University from 1993 to 1996 where he graduated with honors from the College of Law.

From 1998 to 2004 Jim was the commercial department managing attorney at Martin & Seibert, LC practicing in the areas of commercial and consumer litigation, commercial leases, insurance subrogation, and bankruptcy litigation. Jim supervised four attorneys and thirty- plus support staff with over 85,000 open files. attorneys.name: Armand I. Judah
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
For over 40 years, Armand I. Judah has been engaged in the general practice of law, with broad experience in all facets of family law, federal criminal law, business law, probate, civil litigation, and personal injury. He has conducted jury trials in both state and federal courts. Armand delivers full-service legal expertise, providing every client with personalized attention and individualized solutions.

Armand is well-versed in all aspects of family litigation, including divorce, custody, visitation, adoption, and child support. Armand is also a trained mediator who is appointed by the court to mediate in many family court matters. He applies his experience as a mediator by using his negotiation skills to the fullest for his clients. While most issues are resolved through negotiation and mediation, Armand is also prepared to aggressively litigate on behalf of his clients. Armand’s responsibilities as a court-appointed attorney for children in dependency/neglect/abuse cases gives him an extra advantage in handling family law cases, as he has a deep understanding of the family court dynamic and how family issues can affect children.

Armand is an expert in federal criminal defense. In addition to his valuable negotiation skills, Armand’s trial preparation is first-rate. During his career, he has handled numerous complex cases. He has successfully represented individuals in all forms of criminal cases.

In 2010, Armand earned a LEO Weekly Magazine Readers’ Choice Award for Best Attorney, and Judah Law Offices placed in the Top 3 Law Firms in that poll.

Outside the courtroom, Armand has served as volunteer legal counsel for the Louisville Jaycees, the Kentucky Jaycees, and the J. Graham Brown School. He has shared his knowledge as an adjunct professor at the University of Louisville Paralegal Studies Program, Sullivan College Paralegal Institute, and Watterson College Business School. He is a frequent guest lecturer at continuing education seminars for attorneys. His experience as an attorney for children serves him well in his volunteer position on the Board of Directors of the Home of the Innocents. He is also on the Board of Directors of the Peterson-Dumesnil House.

He enjoys assisting his clients in disputes involving breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duty, trade secrets, fraud, business torts, and shareholder rights. David’s clients value his loyalty, tactical skills, aggressiveness, and ability to problem-solve in complex circumstances. attorneys.bio:
William Kautz has been with Edwards and Kautz since its beginning in 2007. He joined with Mark because of Mark Edward’s reputation as a successful and experienced Personal Injury attorney. He enjoys the challenges of helping people as a criminal defense attorney.

William is a partner at the firm and focuses his practice on criminal defense. He believes in the pursuit of Justice. And he has prosecuted and defended hundreds of cases from DUI to capital murder. During that time he has been a prosecutor, a public defender and private lawyer. He has appeared in both Federal and State Courts.

William graduated from law school at Salmon P. Chase in 1978. He graduated from Northern Kentucky University in 1975 with Bachelor of Science in Business. He served as McCracken County Bar Association President.

William is married to Latisha Kinsey Kautz. He has two children. Charlie is now a Chiropractor and Sami works in the hotel industry. He enjoys boating, traveling and playing golf.

Moyer Fellowship for her research into the intersection between wrongful conviction and the deaf and hearing-impaired community.

Haley is licensed to practice in Kentucky Courts. She is a member of the Kentucky Bar Association and the Louisville Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Thomas N. Kerrick
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Bowling Green, KY
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from law school, Tom started working on insurance defense cases. He gained a reputation as a skilled trial lawyer, handling various types of cases such as car accidents, slip-and-falls, arsons, construction claims and products liability. Tom's ability to connect with jurors led other attorneys to refer clients with personal injury claims to him.

Tom has successfully represented clients on both sides of the courtroom. He sincerely believes that trying cases from both perspectives allows him to more thoroughly and objectively guide his clients through litigation. His experience representing both plaintiffs and defendants, along with his reputation for reasonableness, has led to a successful practice as a mediator.

At a young age, Tom achieved an AV Preeminent* rating through Martindale-Hubbell, which he still holds. He has been acknowledged in The Best Lawyers in America publication and was nominated for the esteemed position of 2020 President of the Kentucky Bar Association. Additionally, he has served as a Special Justice to the Kentucky Supreme Court and had the privilege of writing the opinion.

Tom is an active alumnus of the University of Kentucky J. David Rosenberg College of Law. He serves as a director for the College of Law Alumni Board. He was the president of the Alumni Association from 1997-2000. Tom is involved in the Bowling Green community, serving on various boards such as Crimestoppers, Fellowship of Christian Athletes (FCA), Rotary, and Leadership Bowling Green Alumni Association. In 2020, he had the honor of serving as the president of the Kentucky Bar Association.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ falls into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.name: Caitlin P. Kidd
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Caitlin P. Kidd (Caitlin Kidd-Leonard) joined the firm in December 2025. She grew up in Floyd County in Eastern Kentucky and moved to Louisville for her undergraduate studies at the University of Louisville’s Business school, focusing on Marketing and Management. She fell in love with the city, making it her home, and continued her studies at the Brandeis School of Law where she graduated with honors in her class.

During law school, Caitlin held many leadership roles, including Editor-in-Chief for the Journal of Animal and Environmental Law and the Vice President of the Appalachian Law Caucus. She also met her husband, Tom Leonard, in law school, and they reside in Louisville with their tri-colored corgi, Stevie (named after Caitlin’s favorite artist, Stevie Nicks of Fleetwood Mac).

Her law practice primarily focuses on estate planning, probate, adult and minor guardianships, and domestic relations matters in Kentuckiana (including, but not limited to, custody, divorces, support, and adoptions).She was admitted to the Kentucky bar in 2020 and the Indiana bar shortly thereafter in 2021.

Caitlin has been recognized as a “Rising Star” by Super Lawyers and was named as “20 People to Know in Law” by Louisville Business First. She brings empathy and compassion to her work, which is a lost practice at times in the law. Caitlin ensures that her clients are heard, seen, and appreciated during their representation.

In her free time, Caitlin enjoys cycling, watching cooking and reality competition shows, listening to music, and spending time with Tom, Stevie, and her friends and family. She avidly cheers on the UofL Cards, the Cleveland Browns, and the Cincinnati Reds.

Awards and Honors

attorneys.name: Shannon King
attorneys.practice_type: Auto Accidents Lawyers in Henderson, KY
attorneys.bio:
I am a tri-state native who grew up in Newburgh, Indiana. After graduating from Castle High School in 2009, I chose to continue my education at Indiana University in Bloomington. While attending college at Indiana University, I received a Bachelor of Science degree in Public Affairs after many semesters spent on the Dean's List. I was also part of the IU Dance Program and their INMOTION Dance Company.

After completing my undergraduate program, I studied at the McKinney School of Law at Indiana University in Indianapolis. I frequented the Dean's List there as well, even being awarded a Criminal Law Certificate before graduating in 2018-all while being employed as a cheerleader for the NFL's Indianapolis Colts!

I am currently licensed to practice law in Indiana and Kentucky, as well as the U.S. District Courts for the Southern District of Indiana and Western District of Kentucky, and the U.S. 6th Circuit Court of Appeals. Before joining the Curt Hamilton Injury Law team in 2019, I worked at the Indiana Prosecuting Attorney's Council (IPAC).

When I'm not in the office, I love cheering on my favorite team (the University of Kentucky-go Cats!), playing with my black lab, Wrigley, and going horseback riding!

attorneys.name: Harold L. Kirtley II
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse and Neglect Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Hal is a partner at O'Brien Batten Kirtley & Coomer, PLLC. Oral advocacy, particularly trial practice, is a passion of his. He has experience successfully trying civil and criminal cases, and he has successfully argued before the Kentucky Supreme Court. Hal is licensed to practice in Kentucky, as well as the U.S. District Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Kentucky and the Sixth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. He is AV Preeminent peer-review rated through Martindale-Hubbell.*

Hal handles primarily nursing home abuse and neglect cases and medical negligence cases. He enjoys, and considers it a privilege, being a voice in the case for an injured person and his/her family members, whose lives have been forever changed due to improper care.

Hal graduated from the University of Tennessee College of Law (Order of Barristers) in 2003, where he received the McClung Medal, which is awarded to the outstanding advocate of each graduating class. He was elected chair of the Moot Court Board. He was also a two-year member of the National Trial Team, which reached the national finals. Hal also received the 2002 Pryor Award of Excellence in Advocacy. Hal attended the University of Kentucky for college. He received a Bachelor of Arts in journalism in 1999 and a Bachelor of Science in agriculture in 2000.

Hal and his wife are the proud parents of twins (one boy and one girl). He has served as an elder at his church. He enjoys traveling and spending time with his family.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer-review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings™ fall into two categories - legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.name: Stephen A. Klausing Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Birth Injuries Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
In law school, Steve quickly determined that specializing as a trial lawyer in personal injury cases was his calling. After graduating as one of the top ten students in his class, he has since dedicated his entire career to representing personal injury victims. He deeply empathizes with his clients and values the friendships he builds with them over the course of their cases. For Steve, there is no greater honor than making a difference in his clients' lives by obtaining the compensation they deserve. Steve has procured numerous successful outcomes for his clients.

Steve was elected to the Kentucky Justice Association's Leadership Academy - an organization dedicated to protecting the rights of personal injury victims and providing dynamic leadership to the legal profession and the Commonwealth of Kentucky. He has also been selected to 2021 Super Lawyers Rising Stars, recognized by the American Institute of Personal Injury Attorneys as a "10 Best Attorney High Verdict & Settlement Winner," and honored by the National Trial Lawyers as the "Top 40 Under 40" Civil-Plaintiff lawyers in Kentucky.

Steve has been admitted to practice in all of Kentucky's state trial courts, the Kentucky Court of Appeals, the Kentucky Supreme Court, the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky, and the United States District Court for the Western District of Kentucky. Steve has effectively presented oral arguments at the Kentucky appellate level. He has also been admitted to practice pro hac vice in Ohio, Indiana, and West Virginia.

Outside of court, you might find Steve playing basketball, tennis, or racquetball. He enjoys watching sporting events, movies, and spending time with family and friends. In addition, as a hobby, he rehabilitates/improves distressed single-family residential homes.

Steve is always more than happy to speak to clients and potential clients regarding their claims in order to address their questions and ease their concerns. You can rest assured that he will work tirelessly on your case and provide the quality legal representation that you deserve. Please call Steve anytime for a free consultation. We believe that you will find that he is the right trial attorney for you.

Marvin Knorr limits his practice to several key areas of law: criminal defense, family, estate, and business. attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Termination and Retaliation Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Tyler is originally from the West Coast (Washington State, to be exact) and he moved to Kentucky in 2008. Tyler attended law school at the University of Louisville, where he graduated cum laude in the top 10% of his class, was named a Brandeis Scholar, and competed on the Kaufman Securities Moot Court Team in New York City. Tyler was also able to put his business entrepreneurship undergraduate degree to use by participating in U of L's entrepreneurship clinic, which assisted start-up businesses with their legal issues.

Tyler has been practicing employment and business law since before he graduated from law school. He began working with a boutique employment law firm in Louisville out of law school, where he was named a partner in 2015, just two years out of law school. Among his accomplishments, Tyler was lead counsel on a race discrimination class action that recovered over one million dollars for the class members and his efforts have led to millions of dollars in recoveries for individual plaintiffs.

After living in Lexington and commuting to Louisville for several years. Since 2018 Tyler has worked with Robert Roark at the firm and is now a partner in Roark & Korus, PLLC,

Tyler was recognized as a "Rising Star" by Super Lawyers in 2018 and 2019, and he is a Lifetime Member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum.

In his spare time, Tyler is actively involved with his "little" brother through Big Brothers Big Sisters, and donates his efforts to Court Appointed Special Advocates, which is an organization dedicated to assisting childhood victims of abuse and neglect. Tyler is an avid tennis player, snowboarder, and occasionally plays golf until he is reminded how terrible his game is. Tyler also loves music (the SiriusXM Lithium channel is a favorite), and has been playing video games since original Nintendo.

attorneys.name: Whitney True Lawson
attorneys.practice_type: State Criminal Defense Lawyers in Frankfort, KY
attorneys.bio:
Whitney True Lawson was born in Frankfort, Kentucky and attended Franklin County Public Schools until she graduated from Western Hills High School with a 4.0 GPA. Thereafter, she attended Transylvania University and graduated, cum laude, with a Bachelor of Arts Degree in German. While at Transylvania University, she was an active member of her sorority, Phi Mu. Between her junior and senior year at Transylvania University, she interned with former United States Representative, A.B. Chandler, in his Washington, D.C. office. Witnessing the legislative process up-close encouraged her to pursue a law degree.

After Transylvania University, she attended the University of Louisville Brandeis School of Law, where she obtained her Juris Doctorate (J.D.) While studying at University of Louisville, Whitney was a member of University of Louisville Law Review and University of Louisville Moot Court Board. She participated in a number of moot court competitions, including two prestigious Moot Court Competitions involving Trademark Law. She was a semi-finalist at the Pirtle-Washer Oral Argument Trademark Competition in 2011. Also, Whitney and her partner won the national Saul Lefkowitz Trademark Moot Court Competition in Washington, D.C., where they competed against law schools from across the United States.

After law school, Whitney moved to Frankfort with her husband, Philip C. Lawson, where she began practicing with the firm and her father, J. Guthrie True. Whitney specializes in cases involving state criminal law, federal criminal law, domestic relations, disability law, and administrative law. She has represented clients throughout the judicial process, including and through jury trial. Her most recent high-profile case involved her representation of Toby Curtsinger, the main defendant involved with the “Pappy-gate” case before the Franklin Circuit Court. She has also represented clients before the Kentucky Court of Appeals and the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit.

Additionally, Whitney has been appointed as a member of the Criminal Justice Act Panel for the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky, which is a small panel of private lawyers appointed by the court to represent indigent clients in criminal cases before the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky.

Outside of her law practice, Whitney is a member of First United Methodist Church in Frankfort, Kentucky, where she serves as the chairman of the Wesley Center Day School Committee. She enjoys spending time with her husband and their son, exercising, skiing, and spending time with family and friends.

attorneys.name: Philip C. Lawson
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Criminal Defense Lawyers in Frankfort, KY
attorneys.bio:
Philip Coleman Lawson was born in Pineville, Kentucky. Both his parents, William and Susan Lawson, practiced law in southeast Kentucky. He attended high school at The McCallie School in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Thereafter, he attended Centre College in Danville, Kentucky.

At Centre, he was a member of the Varsity Baseball and Golf Teams. He was an active member of his fraternity, Sigma Alpha Epsilon. During the summer before his senior year, Philip interned for former United States Representative, A.B. ("Ben") Chandler, III in his Washington, D.C. office. During the internship, Philip drafted legislation, prepared and participated in presentations to Congressman Chandler and other interested parties regarding proposed legislation, and worked alongside office staff regarding constituent services. He also met his now wife, and law partner, Whitney True Lawson, during this internship.

The experience convinced Philip, and his future wife Whitney, to pursue a legal career. After graduating with a Bachelor of Arts Degree in History with a minor in Government, Philip enrolled at the University of Louisville, Brandeis School of Law. While at UofL, Philip was an active member of the Moot Court Board and UofL's Kentucky Intrastate Mock Trial Team. Philip also clerked for a mid-size firm in Louisville, Kentucky and former Chief Judge Hon. Sara W. Combs of the Kentucky Court of Appeals in Frankfort, Kentucky.

After law school, Philip moved to Frankfort, Kentucky with Whitney to became a Trial Attorney with the Department of Public Advocacy in the Frankfort, Kentucky office. At the DPA, Philip represented hundreds of clients in over a thousand cases ranging from minor traffic infractions and DUI's in District Court to serious felonies in Circuit Court. Philip also represented clients in Juvenile Court and Family Court.

Two years later, Philip joined a large statewide firm in Lexington, Kentucky where he continued to practice state law criminal defense. He also expanded his practice to include insurance defense, federal criminal defense, personal injury, and complex civil litigation.

In 2017, Philip joined Whitney and his father-in-law, J. Guthrie True, at True Guarnieri Ayer, LLP in Frankfort, Kentucky. He was named partner two years later in 2019. Philip continues to represent clients in state law criminal defense, federal criminal defense, personal injury, family law, and complex civil litigation in Frankfort, Kentucky and throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky.

Also since 2020, Philip has represented the Kentucky Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (KACDL) as its legislative agent before the General Assembly. As KACDL’s lobbyist, Philip tracks all proposed legislation involving the criminal justice system. He regularly meets and corresponds with members of both the House and Senate regarding legislative issues. The work also entails drafting, revising, or commenting upon legislation when necessary.

Outside the office, Philip enjoys golf, duck hunting, University of Kentucky athletics, and Cincinnati Reds baseball. Furthermore, he enjoys watching his young son, Henry, play several competitive sports including basketball, baseball, wrestling, and golf.

At the DPA, Philip represented hundreds of clients in over a thousand cases ranging from minor traffic infractions and DUI's in District Court to serious felonies in Circuit Court. Philip also represented clients in Juvenile Court and Family Court.

Two years later, Philip joined a large statewide firm in Lexington, Kentucky where he continued to practice state law criminal defense. He also expanded his practice to include insurance defense, federal criminal defense, personal injury, and complex civil litigation.

In 2017, Philip joined Whitney and his father-in-law, J. Guthrie True, at True Guarnieri Ayer, LLP in Frankfort, Kentucky. He was named partner two years later in 2019. Philip continues to represent clients in state law criminal defense, federal criminal defense, personal injury, family law, and complex civil litigation in Frankfort, Kentucky and throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky.

Also since 2020, Philip has represented the Kentucky Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (KACDL) as its legislative agent before the General Assembly. As KACDL’s lobbyist, Philip tracks all proposed legislation involving the criminal justice system. He regularly meets and corresponds with members of both the House and Senate regarding legislative issues. The work also entails drafting, revising, or commenting upon legislation when necessary.

Outside the office, Philip enjoys golf, duck hunting, University of Kentucky athletics, and Cincinnati Reds baseball. Furthermore, he enjoys watching his young son, Henry, play several competitive sports including basketball, baseball, wrestling, and golf.

attorneys.name: Michael Leigh
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate & Constitutional Law Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Michael Leigh's nationwide practice focuses on complex civil litigation, class and derivative action litigation, and wealth and investment management litigation and arbitration. He represents publicly traded and privately held companies in corporate governance, securities, and commercial litigation, and advises companies and individuals in internal corporate and regulatory investigations.

Michael has represented Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 companies in internal and regulatory investigations involving a wide variety of issues, including embezzlement; fraud; restatement of company financials and SEC filings; foreign corruption and bribery, including the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA); commercial bribery; and unauthorized access to telecommunications and computer systems. He has represented clients in investigations by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), the U.S. Congress, various U.S. Attorney offices and state attorneys general offices, and the U.K. Parliament.

Michael routinely represents broker-dealers and financial advisors in Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) arbitrations and investigations. He also represents registered investment advisers (RIAs) in securities compliance, disclosure requirements, and state and federal audits and investigations.

Michael also represents individuals, boards, and companies in class and derivative actions, fiduciary duty litigation, M&A litigation, trade secrets litigation, consumer class actions, and white-collar criminal defense and investigations. He has represented numerous clients in contract and commercial disputes, in particular disputes involving financial products and highly regulated industries.

Prior to joining the firm, Michael was an associate and partner at the large regional law firm Stites & Harbison PLLC (2015-2018). He also was an associate (2010-2014) at the international law firm Debevoise and Plimpton LLP in New York. Michael served from 2013-2014 as a Special Assistant Federal Defender in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York where he was court-appointed counsel for criminal defendants. He currently serves as a Criminal Justice Act counsel, assigned by the United States District Court for the Western District of Kentucky to represent indigent persons charged with federal crimes.

In addition to his practice, Michael is an adjunct professor at the University of Louisville Brandeis School of Law, where he teaches Securities Regulation.

Kelli is a proud Hilltopper, having graduated from Western Kentucky University magna cum laude. While attending the University of Kentucky School of Law, she received numerous awards for her trial advocacy skills and was chosen to be an editor for the Kentucky Journal of Equine, Agriculture and Natural Resources Law.

Kelli has dedicated her life to representing individuals who have been injured as a result of car crashes. She has tried a number of cases successfully to verdict in Kentucky and has obtained numerous seven-figure settlements when the insurance companies offered $0 prior to litigation. She grew up in a very small town, which continues to drive her passion for helping everyday people who are taken advantage of by insurance companies.

When Kelli isn't working she enjoys being with her husband, Chase and two daughters, Lane and Lola.

attorneys.name: Hollie B. Lindsey
attorneys.practice_type: Wills Trusts and Probate Lawyers in Hartford, KY
attorneys.bio:
As a native of Ohio County, I consider it an honor to help my friends and neighbors in our local community with their legal needs. I assist clients during some of the most difficult times of their lives whether it be probating an estate, transitioning through the immigration process, guiding them after suffering an injury, or other significant milestones in life.

The legal system can often be overwhelming for many people. I take the time to explain to my clients the process of events that will occur in their case and let them know I will be with them every step of the way.

My undergraduate studies were completed in 2003 at the University of Kentucky. After graduation I worked as a Constituent Service Representative for Kentucky's Senior United States Senator, Mitch McConnell. While working for the Senator I realized that a law degree would provide more opportunities to make a difference in people's lives. I graduated law school in 2009 and was delighted when Foreman Watson Holtrey, LLP offered me a position in my hometown, allowing me to practice law in a community that means so much to me.

My husband and I have twins - a boy and a girl - that always make sure we live life to the fullest outside of the office. We are happy to be raising our children in such a fine community amongst such fine people.

attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Mike is the chief civil litigation attorney at The Nye Law Group, P.C. He has over 23 years of personal injury litigation experience and is AV Preeminent Peer Review Rated by Martingale Hubbell.

Mike began his legal career as an insurance defense litigation attorney. Eventually he felt compelled to assist the injured instead of the big insurance companies and became a plaintiffs' attorney. Before joining The Nye Law Group, P.C., Mike was a litigation attorney with Gary C. Johnson, PSC. Mike recently obtained a 1.68 million dollar jury verdict from a medical negligence case. Mike has a solid track record for obtaining the compensation that his clients need and deserve.

Mike's primary area of practice includes: wrongful death, motor vehicle/trucking accidents, nursing home negligence, medical negligence, premises liability, and several MDL (multi district litigation) cases including DePuy, TVM, HRT, and Vioxx. Mike is a member of the American Bar Association's Tort Trial and Insurance Practice Section, Plaintiff's Policy Task Force Leadership Member, Healthcare Law Section, Litigation Section and American Association for Justice. Mike is licensed to practice law in Georgia and Kentucky.

Mike resides in the Hilton Head area with his wife, Missy, and five children. In his free time, Mike enjoys spending time with his family, sports, and physical fitness.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Danville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Rami Little started her own firm in 2018. She concentrates her law practice in the area of Family Law, handling all types of matters including adoptions, divorce, child custody, dependency, neglect and abuse, single sex couples or other parties who have been placed in a parent-like role and all other aspects of domestic litigation. In these cases she strives to help individuals and families through the process in a compassionate manner.

Rami also has extensive experience in defending those charged with a crime. She worked as an Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney in Fayette County for Commonwealth Attorney Ray Larson until 2007. During her time at the Commonwealth Attorney's office, she prosecuted and tried all types of felony cases including Murder, Rape, Child Sexual Abuse, Burglary, Theft and Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol. Since becoming a private practice attorney, she has been able to bring her criminal prosecution experience to her to defend her clients.

Rami lives in Danville KY with her four sons and husband Brian. Outside of work, Rami is active part of the community. She is an active parishioner at Sts. Peter and Paul Catholic Church. Further, Rami is a member of the Boyle County Middle School PTO. She also serves on the board of the Hudson-Ellis Foundation and is a former board member of the Wilderness Trace Child Development Center and the Family Services Association. Rami was recently selected to serve on the Kentucky Bar Association Rules Committee.

Rami is a Cuban-American who is a native Spanish speaker and enjoys working with members of the Spanish speaking community. She currently serves on the Centro Latino Board.

attorneys.practice_type: Labor & Employment Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Amanda Lockaby is currently the Co-Managing Partner at Lockaby PLLC and was formerly a partner at an AmLaw 200 firm. She has extensive experience defending personal injury and product liability claims, including the successful defense of complex multi-district litigation, on behalf of businesses of all sizes, including product designers and manufacturers, long-term care providers, national retailers, and utility contractors. Amanda also defends employers against all kinds of discrimination, retaliation, harassment, and wage-and-hour actions and provides day-to-day HR and contract counsel to owners, business unit leaders, and human resources professionals. Amanda serves as the Vice Chair for the Ambassador Board of Lexington Habitat for Humanity, and is a volunteer for Legal Aid of the Bluegrass in their Domestic Violence Advocacy Program. Outside the office she enjoys traveling, being outdoors, and spending time with her children, Lily and Aidan.

attorneys.name: Matthew T. Lockaby
attorneys.practice_type: Labor & Employment Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
The managing partner of Lockaby PLLC, Matt maintains a diverse practice that stems from his joy working with small business. For nearly two decades, Matt has provided strategic advice and counsel to businesses of all sizes, from startups to Fortune 500 companies, to resolve the myriad day-to-day HR and personnel issues that arise during the employment lifespan, from recruiting and hiring to termination, layoffs, and reductions in force—and everything in between. Matt has also fiercely defended employers and management against a wide variety of discrimination, retaliation, harassment, and wage-and-hour claims in state and federal courts, including class-action and FLSA collective-action claims.

Matt has also carved a special niche for non-compete litigation, particularly for startups and their owners, successfully litigating breach-of-contract and breach-of-fiduciary-duty actions in Kentucky and beyond, including federal court in New York and arbitration in Florida.

His work with small business owners extends beyond labor-and-employment guidance, as Matt also provides corporate and transactional expertise and general counsel services, all of which is aided, in no small part, by the fact that he is a small business owner himself—of Lockaby PLLC and of Axis HR Solutions LLC, a human-resources consulting company that provides outsourced HR services and HR and human capital due diligence and integration solutions to buyers and sellers in middle-market M&A transactions.

Matt’s expertise spans the business lifecycle, including entity selection and formation for startups (including the preparation of operating, partnership, and shareholder agreements and related documents); employment, management, and operating contracts (including employment and independent contractor agreements, restrictive covenants, master service agreements, supplier agreements, and vendor agreements); and the purchase and sale of businesses through mergers and acquisitions.

Finally, Matt helps buyers and sellers manage the complex labor-and-employment issues that arise during a merger or acquisition, often working in conjunction with corporate counsel and the entire deal team to help clients achieve the desired transaction goals, minimize the risks inherent in any integration, and ensure compliance with the myriad international, federal, state, and local laws and regulations.

Beyond Lockaby PLLC

Matt resides in Lexington, Kentucky, with his wife and law partner, Amanda, and their two children. Outside the office, you can usually find him outdoors: He has climbed Mt. Kilimanjaro in Tanzania, Africa; Mt. Rainier in Washington; and Quandary Peak in Colorado, and he escapes to Lake Cumberland and the U.S. Virgin Islands to go boating every chance he gets.

attorneys.name: T. Brian Lowder
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Bowling Green, KY
attorneys.bio:
Brian, a Kentucky native, was born in Lexington and grew up in Bowling Green. Following high school, he attended Western Kentucky University, where he played football and was a starting member of the 2002 National Championship team. Brian earned WKU’s Scholar Athlete of the Year Award and was a First Team Academic All-American in 2002. In 2003, he graduated summa cum laude with a major in Political Science and Sociology and a minor in Criminology. With a perfect 4.0 GPA, Brian received the Scholar of the College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences accolade along with the prestigious Ogdens Trustees’ Award. Following college, Brian attended the University of Louisville Brandeis School of Law where he was a member of the Brandeis Law Journal and finished in the top of his class. During law school, Brian enjoyed clerkships with two prominent Louisville law firms. Upon graduation, he returned to Bowling Green to begin his practice with the law firm of Bell, Orr, Ayers, & Moore. Brian practiced in a variety of areas during his association with BOAM, including domestic and family law, personal injury, insurance defense, commercial litigation, real estate litigation, employment law and criminal defense.

In 2009, Brian became a solo practitioner and established The Law Office of T. Brian Lowder, where he practiced in the areas of personal injury, criminal law, domestic and family, and general litigation. In the fall of 2013, Brian and Matt formed Lowder & McGill, with the intention of focusing primarily on serious personal injury cases. Today, the firm continues to pursue the common goal of aggressive representation of their clients’ interests and has recovered millions of dollars on their behalf. Brian is a trial lawyer and extremely familiar with the courtroom. He has tried numerous bench and jury trials to verdict. Although his primary practice area is the representation of plaintiffs in serious injury cases, Brian continues to represent clients in the realm of criminal defense and small businesses in commercial litigation. He has experience representing a client base ranging from hard working, low income earners to professional athletes and entertainers in a variety of litigation. Regardless of who the client is, they receive the same aggressive and candid representation, with their interests at the forefront.

Brian is married to Beth Lowder and they have two children, Conor and Collins. In addition to practicing law, Brian enjoys coaching his children in sports, investing in real estate, trying to learn to play golf and spending time outdoors. He currently serves on the WKU Hilltopper Foundation Executive Board, the Bowling Green-Warren County Historic Preservation Board and the WKU W-Club Board.

attorneys.name: Joanne Lynch
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Joanne Lynch represents people, organizations, and businesses throughout Kentucky and Indiana, bringing substantial experience in litigation, negotiation, and legal and practical counseling to her clients. She focuses her practice on administrative law, family law, criminal defense, wills and probate, appellate law, and sports law.

Listening to clients, understanding their goals, and developing effective strategies to achieve those goals are at the center of Joanne’s work. Whether a legal issue needs to be addressed through negotiation, trial, hearing, mediation, investigation, or all the above, Joanne can do it while relying on her experiences in hundreds of negotiations, mediations, and trials in Kentucky and Indiana.

Joanne served as a public defender in Kentucky for 15 years, concentrating during the last 10 years on defending people in death-penalty-eligible cases. She helped her clients navigate challenging factual circumstances and complex legal issues in stressful times.

Outside of the office, Joanne enjoys playing tennis, birdwatching, and volunteering with her neighborhood association. She cheers for the Louisville Cardinals, Racing Louisville, and safe trips and happy retirements for all Thoroughbred racehorses.

attorneys.bio:
Ed Massey is a Northern Kentucky native living in Boone County with his wife, Anita. He is a proud father of three daughters and grandfather to two grandchildren. attorneys.name: Jeffrey K. McClain
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration & Naturalization Law Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey K. McClain's practice is concentrated in Immigration. His practice includes family-based immigration and employment-based immigration cases, as well as Removal and Deportation cases. In addition to his employment-based immigration practice, Mr. McClain assists employers with employment verification and compliance issues including I-9 audits and reviews. His clients consist of families, individuals, private employers, religious organizations, private primary and secondary schools and institutions of higher education.

Mr. McClain began his practice at the Catholic Charities Office of Immigrant Services. While practicing at the Catholic Charities, he represented numerous refugees who fled their home countries for fear of persecution. He also represented foreign nationals and their U.S. citizen family members with family-based petitions and applications.

After leaving the Catholic Charities, Mr. McClain worked at one of the large regional law firms and a medium-sized local law firm where he continued his focus in Immigration and Nationality Law. At both firms, he continued to represent employers and employees in employment-based immigration cases before the U.S. Citizenship & Immigration Services, U.S. Department of State and U.S. Department of Labor. Here, Mr. McClain's work focused on temporary visas for foreign workers, including H-1B, L-1, E-2, TN, R-1, O-1/O-2 and P-1/P-2 visas among other employment-based non-immigrant visas. Mr. McClain also represented employers and employees with permanent labor certification (PERM) and immigrant petitions for foreign workers. In addition to his employment-based immigration practice, Mr. McClain continued representing families and individuals in filing petitions and applications for family members, permanent residency and citizenship.

Mr. McClain's practice also included representing employers with workplace and worksite compliance where he conducted I-9 audits and employment compliance reviews with employers. This work included representing clients before the U.S. Department of Labor in prevailing wage disputes before the Wage and Hour Division and debarment cases before the Administrative Law Judges.

Mr. McClain also served as a state prosecutor with the Jefferson County Attorney's Office in Louisville, Kentucky. There, he was assigned to the Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Unit where he prosecuted crimes of domestic violence ranging from assault to stalking. He also served in the Felony/Misdemeanor Division where he prosecuted crimes ranging from non-domestic assault, financial crimes, fraud and drugs.

Mr. McClain has given numerous presentations and Continuing Legal Education Programs on Immigration and Nationality Law over the years to a multitude of organizations ranging from the Louisville Bar Association, Women's Law Enforcement Network, Foreign Student Advisors, Student Organizations, Construction Organizations and various other social groups. Mr. McClain has also served as an Adjunct Professor at the Louis D. Brandeis School of Law at the University of Louisville where he taught Immigration Law.

attorneys.name: Steven M. McCauley Esq., MBA
attorneys.practice_type: Securities Law Matters Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
A native of Lexington, Kentucky, Mr. McCauley has been an attorney with Charles C. Mihalek, PSC for nearly 20 years. He has represented hundreds of aggrieved investors in disputes against the Securities broker-dealers, banks, registered investment advisors and the financial advisors employed thereby. Mr. McCauley graduated from the University of Kentucky in 1987 and received his law degree (J.D.) from the University of Kentucky, College of Law in 1990. He also holds an MBA in Finance which he received (with distinction) from the University of Kentucky College of Business and Economics in 1992. Mr. McCauley is admitted to practice in all courts of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, the U.S. Supreme Court, the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States District Courts in the Western and Eastern Districts of Kentucky. Mr. McCauley serves as both an Arbitrator and Panel Chairperson for the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

Mr. McCauley is an active member of the Kentucky Bar Association, where he currently serves as Vice Chair on the Alternative Dispute Resolution Section. Mr. McCauley is a member of the Fayette County Bar Association, and the Public Investors Arbitration Bar Association (PIABA), an international bar association dedicated to protecting and representing investors in securities and commodities arbitration proceedings brought against the securities industry.

Mr. McCauley focuses his practice on investor rights and securities law matters, including securities arbitrations and litigation, SEC and FINRA enforcement matters, employment disputes, securities class actions, and complex civil litigation. He has presented investment seminars and is the co-author of “Why Statutes of Limitations Are Not Applicable in Kentucky Arbitration,” Kentucky Bar Association Bench & Bar Magazine, March 2011.

attorneys.name: Terrence L. McCoy
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
We were married in 1967 in Princeton, NJ and started shortly thereafter to train for the Peace Corps. We served with the Peace Corps in the Independent State of Western Samoa. While in Samoa I worked in the Attorney General's office and with the Law Draftsman. While there I learned about customary Samoan laws, and the Lands & Titles Court which was set up by the Germans after they took control in the late 19th century. When New Zealand became the Trustee of Samoa under the League of Nations it introduced the statutory law of New Zealand which is based on the Common Law. We left Samoa in 1970, travelling home via the Cook Islands, Tonga, Fiji, New Zealand, Australia, Djibouti, Greece, Switzerland, Germany, France and the UK.

I started practicing law with my father in 1970 and Martha started medical school. She is now retired from a general surgical practice and I achieved senior counsel status in 2016. We celebrated our fiftieth wedding anniversary on August 26, 2017. For the last twenty-three years Martha and I have had an ownership interest in a farm in the Dordogne region of France. As a result of this I have had a chance to get a glimpse of law based on the Napoleonic Code. As a result of these experiences, I have learned that the " law" means various things in different parts of the world.

attorneys.name: William F. McGee Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Smithland, KY
attorneys.bio:
William F. McGee Jr. is a veteran civil and criminal defense trial attorney. Members of the legal bar and judges have rated attorney McGee as AV Preeminent®: The highest peer rating standard. This is given to attorneys who are ranked at the highest level of professional excellence for their legal expertise, communication skills, and ethical standards by their peers.[1][2]

Mr. McGee has a track record of successful outcomes in cases including, but not limited to, personal injury awards, divorces, will contests, land disputes, misdemeanors, DUIs, felony assaults, felony sex crimes, felony drug charges and several highly publicized murder cases throughout Western Kentucky.

Over the last 30 years, Mr. McGee has secured numerous “NOT GUILTY” Jury Verdicts for clients charged with crimes such as, but not limited to, First Degree Murder, Drug Offenses, Assaults, Felony Sex offenses, DUIs, and other felonies and misdemeanors.

Many of Mr. McGee’s clients have had criminal charges “DISMISSED” when charged with crimes such as First Degree Murder, Manslaughter, Attempted Murder, First Degree Trafficking, First Degree Possession, Felony Sex offenses, Felony assault offenses, Felony Wanton Endangerment, Felony Neglect, Felony Burglary, Convicted Felon with Firearm Possession, Theft offenses, Unlawful Transactions with a minor, DUI, EPO/DVO violations, Terroristic Threatening, Menacing, Criminal Trespass, Misdemeanor Wanton Endangerment, Misdemeanor Assault, Resisting Arrest, Unlawful Taking of Wildlife, and many other felonies and misdemeanors.

Beyond "Not Guilty" verdicts and "Dismissals," Mr. McGee has successfully represented many clients before the Kentucky Supreme Court and Kentucky Court of Appeals. and the UNITED STATES SUPREME COURT. To his credit, Mr. McGee’s work in these courts has resulted in changes to existing law or the creation of new law in the Commonwealth of Kentucky. Today, lawyers and judges throughout Kentucky often look to the published decisions in Mr. McGee’s cases for guidance. For his clients, Mr. McGee’s work has resulted in favorable, published decisions in legal areas including, but not limited to, (1) a murder defendant’s right to test evidence, (2) a drug trafficking charge’s dismissal due to an illegal search, (3) a wrongful death action against an insurance company, (4) a certified public accountant husband’s misappropriation of over $2,000,000.00 in a divorce, and (5) a challenge to a widow’s claim to land and money valued at over $850,000.00.

Mr. McGee is committed to getting great outcomes for clients by keeping them informed at every stage of the process. He is a third-generation attorney preceded in the office by his grandfather, Raymond B. Dycus, and father, William F. McGee. He is admitted to practice in all Kentucky state courts and the United States District Court for the Western District of Kentucky.

Successful Criminal Defense, Divorce, Personal Injury and Trial Attorney

Mr. McGee has decades of experience, and his reputation accurately reflects his elite legal skills. He has a nationally recognized record of peer-reviewed distinction. Through his advocacy, he has established new case law and is always looking for new and innovative ways to defend and assert his clients' rights.

THE FOLLOWING CASES ARE "PUBLISHED" APPELLATE COURT CASES ESTABLISHING, CLARIFYING OR MODIFYING THE LAW IN THE COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY HANDLED BY ATTORNEY MCGEE: L.O. v. Commonwealth of Kentucky, 995 SW2d 384 (Ky. 1999) (favorable decision - first degree murder); Commonwealth of Kentucky v. McManus, 107 SW3d 175 (Ky. 2003) (US Supreme Court certioria denied) (favorable decision - drug trafficking); General Accident Ins. Co. of America v. Guess, 936 SW2d 97 (Ky.Ct.App. 1997) (favorable decision - wrongful death); Kleet v. Kleet, 264 SW3d 610 (Ky.Ct.App. 2007) (favorable decision - divorce); Vick v. Elliot, 422 S.W.3d 277 (Ky.Ct. App. 2014) (favorable decision - real estate), Marshall v. Marshall, 599 S.W.3d 381 (Ky.Ct. App. 2018) (favorable decision - family law).

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
William F. McGee Jr. is a veteran civil and criminal defense trial attorney. Members of the legal bar and judges have rated attorney McGee as AV Preeminent®: The highest peer rating standard. This is given to attorneys who are ranked at the highest level of professional excellence for their legal expertise, communication skills, and ethical standards by their peers.[1][2]

Mr. McGee has a track record of successful outcomes in cases including, but not limited to, personal injury awards, divorces, will contests, land disputes, misdemeanors, DUIs, felony assaults, felony sex crimes, felony drug charges and several highly publicized murder cases throughout Western Kentucky.

Over the last 30 years, Mr. McGee has secured numerous “NOT GUILTY” Jury Verdicts for clients charged with crimes such as, but not limited to, First Degree Murder, Drug Offenses, Assaults, Felony Sex offenses, DUIs, and other felonies and misdemeanors.

Many of Mr. McGee’s clients have had criminal charges “DISMISSED” when charged with crimes such as First Degree Murder, Manslaughter, Attempted Murder, First Degree Trafficking, First Degree Possession, Felony Sex offenses, Felony assault offenses, Felony Wanton Endangerment, Felony Neglect, Felony Burglary, Convicted Felon with Firearm Possession, Theft offenses, Unlawful Transactions with a minor, DUI, EPO/DVO violations, Terroristic Threatening, Menacing, Criminal Trespass, Misdemeanor Wanton Endangerment, Misdemeanor Assault, Resisting Arrest, Unlawful Taking of Wildlife, and many other felonies and misdemeanors.

Beyond "Not Guilty" verdicts and "Dismissals," Mr. McGee has successfully represented many clients before the Kentucky Supreme Court and Kentucky Court of Appeals. and the UNITED STATES SUPREME COURT. To his credit, Mr. McGee’s work in these courts has resulted in changes to existing law or the creation of new law in the Commonwealth of Kentucky. Today, lawyers and judges throughout Kentucky often look to the published decisions in Mr. McGee’s cases for guidance. For his clients, Mr. McGee’s work has resulted in favorable, published decisions in legal areas including, but not limited to, (1) a murder defendant’s right to test evidence, (2) a drug trafficking charge’s dismissal due to an illegal search, (3) a wrongful death action against an insurance company, (4) a certified public accountant husband’s misappropriation of over $2,000,000.00 in a divorce, and (5) a challenge to a widow’s claim to land and money valued at over $850,000.00.

Mr. McGee is committed to getting great outcomes for clients by keeping them informed at every stage of the process. He is a third-generation attorney preceded in the office by his grandfather, Raymond B. Dycus, and father, William F. McGee. He is admitted to practice in all Kentucky state courts and the United States District Court for the Western District of Kentucky.

Successful Criminal Defense, Divorce, Personal Injury and Trial Attorney

Mr. McGee has decades of experience, and his reputation accurately reflects his elite legal skills. He has a nationally recognized record of peer-reviewed distinction. Through his advocacy, he has established new case law and is always looking for new and innovative ways to defend and assert his clients' rights.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Bowling Green, KY
attorneys.bio:
Stephanie McGehee-Shacklette is an experienced attorney specializing in estate planning, elder law, business representation, and creditor representation. She is an AV-rated lawyer by Martindale-Hubbell, a distinction that reflects the high ethical standards and legal expertise recognized by her peers. Stephanie also holds the distinguished title of Fellow in the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel (ACTEC), an honor recognizing the top estate planning and trust lawyers in the country. Stephanie has built a reputation as a trusted advisor in her field and is known for providing strategic counsel to individuals, families, and businesses across Kentucky.

Since July 1, 2023, Stephanie has served on the Board of Governors of the Kentucky Bar Association, representing the 2nd Supreme Court District. She is dedicated to advancing the legal profession and advocating for the interests of Kentucky attorneys and their clients.

She has held leadership roles in several professional organizations, including serving as the former chair of the South Central Kentucky Estate Planning Council. In addition to her professional work, Stephanie has received numerous accolades for her commitment to public service. She is the recipient of the Gwyneth B. Davis Outstanding Public Service Award and the Pro Bono Public Award from the Warren County Lawyers Care Program for her significant pro bono contributions to the community.

Stephanie has made substantial contributions to legal education, having served on the Planning Committee of the UK/CLE Midwest-Midsouth Estate Planning Institute since 2019. This prestigious, two-day event is the longest-running annual CLE in Kentucky. She is also a sought-after speaker at continuing education events, where she shares her expertise in estate planning, business succession, and trust administration.

Stephanie’s broad expertise and commitment to the legal community and her clients make her a trusted professional in her field. Whether advising clients on estate planning or guiding legal professionals through complex issues, Stephanie’s leadership and contributions continue to make a lasting impact on the legal profession in Kentucky and beyond.

attorneys.name: Matt M. McGill
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Crash Lawyers in Bowling Green, KY
attorneys.bio:
﻿Matt grew up Bowling Green, Kentucky and attended college at Miami University on a partial athletic scholarship. During his Junior year at Miami, Matt took a Business Law course that was taught by a local attorney. It was by far the most interesting course that Matt took in college and laid the foundation for his eventual career in the law. After graduating from Miami with a degree in Accounting and a minor in Political Science, Matt attended the University of Kentucky College of Law. During his third year of law school, Matt worked in the College of Law Legal Clinic, where he handled a number of pro bono cases for clients that couldn’t afford to pay a lawyer. Much of the work involved litigation of civil disputes and piqued his interest in civil litigation and trial work.

Matt obtained his law degree in 2005 and returned to Bowling Green to begin practicing law at a well-respected local firm. During his eight years at that firm, Matt handled a wide variety of cases, ranging from commercial litigation to insurance defense to representing plaintiffs in personal injury and wrongful death claims. Matt gravitated toward representing individuals that were harmed or killed through no fault of their own. He loved helping those clients and found it much more rewarding than the other work he had done.

In 2013, Matt joined his friend and law partner Brian Lowder to found Lowder & McGill, PLLC. Their firm was founded on the principle of aggressive representation of their client’s interest. Matt enjoys the challenge of obtaining justice for his clients, whether it be in reaching a fair settlement or taking the case to trial.

Matt feels that it is his responsibility to give back to the community whenever possible. He is a former member of several civic organizations and has served as a board member for several charitable organizations, including service as President for Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) of South Central KY, an advocacy group that seeks to protect abused and neglected children. Matt and his wife Amy have two beautiful daughters, Vivienne and Susanna.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Martindale AV Preeminent Rating, 2024

Warren County Bar Association - Pro Bono Publico Award, 2022

Kentucky Bar Foundation - Life Fellow, 2015

CASA - Six Years of Outstanding Service, 2018

attorneys.name: Adrian M. Mendiondo
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Adrian Mendiondo grew up in Lexington, Kentucky and has practiced law in Lexington since 2005. After graduating from Henry Clay High School in 1996, Mr. Mendiondo pursued his undergraduate degree from Emory University, in Atlanta, Georgia, and then moved to Los Angeles California to attend Pepperdine University School of Law. Mr. Mendiondo graduated cum laude from Pepperdine in 2003, was admitted to the California bar, and practiced in Los Angeles from 2003 to 2004. He then returned to Lexington where he has practiced since being admitted to the Kentucky Bar in 2005.

Mr. Mendiondo began his Kentucky practice as an associate with Stoll Keenon Ogden; then joined Kinkead & Stilz in 2007. In both firms he focused primarily on business, employment, and civil rights litigation, representing small and large businesses and governmental agencies across Kentucky. Mr. Mendiondo was elected as an equity partner at Kinkead & Stilz in 2010, and continued to work there until he joined Morgan & Morgan in 2015. He came to Morgan and Morgan to switch the focus of his practice from defending business to pursuing claims on behalf of those who've had their civil rights violated.

During his career Mr. Mendiondo has earned substantial litigation experience in federal and state courts across Kentucky. He has successfully tried numerous cases to a jury in both state and federal courts, and has successfully pursued and defended appeals to the Kentucky Court of Appeals and the United States Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals. He is admitted to practice before all states courts in Kentucky and California, the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Kentucky and Central District of California, and the United States Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Mr. Mendiondo is married to Whitney Howard Mendiondo and has two children, Lillian and Anna Claire.
