He is licensed to practice in Kentucky, Ohio, and Indiana, in the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, and in the United States District Courts for the Eastern District of Kentucky, Western District of Kentucky, Southern District of Ohio, and Southern District of Indiana. His practice primarily consists of defending those accused of serious crimes in federal court and representing individuals, businesses, and insurance companies in personal injury cases. He is well-recognized for his abilities, having been named by Super Lawyers as a Rising Star from 2019-2025, and as a Super Lawyer in 2026.

The bulk of his civil practice centers on personal injury and wrongful death cases, with an emphasis on car crashes, slip-and-falls, and dog bites. He is one of the few practitioners in Northern Kentucky who splits his civil practice equally between representing plaintiffs and defendants in personal injury matters, which gives him a balanced insight into how each side approaches these types of cases.

Lee's passion is in his robust criminal defense practice. He routinely defends those accused of serious felony offenses, particularly in federal court. The long and short of it is that you need Lee if you're in “big trouble,” facing lots of time in prison or other serious consequences. Other lawyers often call him for advice on their federal criminal cases. He is a member of the Criminal Justice Act panels for the Southern District of Ohio at Cincinnati and the Eastern District of Kentucky at Covington, and he serves on the CJA Committee as the Panel Representative for the Covington division. He has tried a number of criminal cases designated as “complex” by the federal judiciary. He is one of the only attorneys in the area to have won an acquittal (“not guilty” verdict) in federal court.

He has guided clients through many types of criminal allegations. Examples include:

Arson

Bank robbery

Battery

Bomb threats/terrorism

Child abuse

Child pornography (possession, receipt, and production)

Counterfeiting

Conspiracy

Drug offenses (e.g. methamphetamine, marijuana, heroin, fentanyl, carfentanil, cocaine, crack, and pills/prescription drugs)

False statement in application/use of a passport

Federal crimes

Felon-in-possession of firearm or ammunition

Forfeiture

Fraud (e.g. mail fraud, insurance fraud, tax fraud, business fraud, etc.)

Gun crimes (e.g. machine guns, possession by a felon, possession in furtherance of drug trafficking)

Identity theft

Immigration offenses

Insider trading

Money laundering

Murder/Murder-for-Hire

Overdose resulting in death

Public corruption

Racketeering/RICO conspiracies

Robbery/Hobbs Act Robbery

Sex offenses

Theft offenses

Unlawful distribution of drugs (i.e., "trafficking")

White collar crimes

Lee also handles criminal appeals, 2255 motions, and habeas corpus petitions for post-conviction relief. He is a member of the Criminal Justice Act Panel for the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit and regularly represents indigent defendants in criminal appeals. He also has experience briefing petitions for a writ of certiorari to the United States Supreme Court.

Examples of Lee’s success in the criminal arena include:

Representation of a man who was arrested on I-75 and wrongfully accused of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine in Boone County. Lee tried the case to a jury and obtained a not guilty verdict and complete acquittal. United States v. Oudone Thengkham, Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 2:25-CR-27.

Representation of a defendant who was federally charged in a carfentanil conspiracy that resulted in an overdose death. The mandatory minimum sentence was life imprisonment. Due to Lee's adept management of the case and the filing of several key defensive motions, the charge against his client was dismissed. United States v. Terrill Hill, Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 2:17-CR-10.

Defense of a wrongfully accused individual in a child pornography case. The case was tried, resulting in a hung jury and subsequent dismissal. Commonwealth of Kentucky v. Andrew Stern, Kenton Circuit Court, Case No. 16-CR-841.

Representation of multiple individuals over the years who were sentenced to no prison time despite pleading guilty to federal felony offenses. See, e.g., United States v. John Enlow, Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 2:15-CR-36; United States v. Brandi Bright, Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 2:19-CR-33; United States v. Brian DeLafayette, Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 2:21-CR-27; United States v. Contessa Qualls, Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 2:23-CR-046.

Defense of an innocent man charged with being a felon in possession of a firearm. The case was dismissed after the filing of several defensive motions. United States v. Nephi Mendez, Eastern District of Kentucky, Case No. 2:19-CR-71.

Representation of a defendant on appeal following his guilty plea. The defendant's conviction was vacated due to Lee's argument that the conviction was obtained in violation of the defendant's due process rights. United States v. Jorge Vargas-Ruiz, United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, Case No. 20-5175.

Successful appeal of a sentence upon revocation of supervised release. Lee was able to persuade the Court of Appeals that the district court had improperly calculated the sentencing guidelines range as a matter of law. United States v. Tae’Vontae Miles, United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, Case No. 22-3245.

Obtaining pretrial release for a client charged with a capital offense (i.e., a crime punishable by the death penalty).

Lee also prepares simple wills, living wills, and powers of attorney, and he helps families navigate the probate and estate administration process when a loved one passes away.

attorneys.bio:
For over 20 years, Mason has been winning complex, high-profile cases for both plaintiffs and defendants in state and federal courts throughout the country. Mr. Miller has extensive experience in corporate and other complex commercial litigation, and represents clients in a wide variety of industries and of all different sizes and types, from individuals to start-ups to Fortune 100 companies. He also regularly advises and represents parties in connection with partnership disputes, construction litigation, M&A deal litigation, non-compete litigation, post-closing disputes and breach of contract matters. Mr. Miller received his B.S. from Northwestern University and his J.D. from Washington and Lee University School of Law, where he was an adjunct instructor at the Williams School of Commerce and author of “Techno Liability: Corporate Websites, Hyperlinks, and Rule 10b-5,” Washington & Lee Law Review (2001).

Joy has practiced law in state and federal courts across the Southeast since 2000. She began her legal career as a judicial law clerk, where she gained hands-on experience in all stages of litigation. She later practiced at a prestigious defense firm, where she handled complex commercial litigation matters.

Joy has been active in community service for more than 20 years, with a focus on children and teenagers. After volunteering as a pet therapy handler for pediatric cancer patients, she co-founded Cure KY Kids to provide funding, awareness, and support to children fighting cancer and their families. She also helped create the Curing Childhood Cancer specialty license plate and serves on the Board of Directors for Kids Cancer Alliance.

Joy is happily married to Matt Minner, and they are the proud parents of 4 children.

Matthew Minner is a Lexington personal injury lawyer who was recently named Personal Injury Lawyer of the Year for the Lexington area by Best Lawyers. He serves as Partner and CEO of Minner Vines Injury Lawyers, PLLC, where he leads the firm’s strategic direction while continuing to try major jury trials in both state and federal courts. Over the course of his career, he has handled complex, high-profile cases across the country, securing million- and multi-million-dollar verdicts and settlements for the people he represents.

Lawdragon has recognized Matt as a “Visionary” and one of the nation’s leading legal innovators. His cases have been featured by USA Today, Good Morning America, CBS, ABC, Fox, Law360, and The National Law Journal.

Outside the courtroom, Matt channels that same drive into competition. He has run the Boston Marathon, completed triathlons, coached youth baseball and football, and is currently training for the 29,029-foot “Everesting” challenge.

attorneys.name: Dion Moorman
attorneys.practice_type: Boating Accidents Lawyers in Owensboro, KY
attorneys.bio:
Dion Moorman was born and raised in Owensboro, Kentucky, where he graduated from Owensboro Senior High School. He attended Murray State University and served as a Student Ambassador while receiving the school's Dr. Marvin Mill's Scholarship. Thereafter, he obtained his Juris Doctor from the University of Louisville School of Law, where he served as a member of the Journal of Law and Education.

He practiced law in Louisville for 2 years before returning to his hometown. Shortly after his return to Owensboro, he had the privilege of being trained and mentored by a Kentucky personal injury legend, Charles E. Moore. For 15 years he practiced complex personal injury law in federal and state courts across Western Kentucky. He gained valuable experience in bodily injury cases, including but not limited to the areas of medical malpractice, product liability, premises liability and auto wrecks. Through his litigation experience, he has become aware that each client is different and tailors his approach to each case accordingly.

In addition to practicing law, Dion teaches business law and employment law, as an adjunct professor, at Kentucky Wesleyan College in Owensboro, Kentucky. Also, he serves as a board member of the Owensboro Public School's Foundation of Excellence.

He attends Blessed Mother Catholic Church and has been blessed with two healthy children, Adelyn and Mara, and devotes most of his time away from the practice of law on activities with the kids.

Awards and Honors

Honors

attorneys.bio:
Douglas H. Morris was born and raised in Dawson Springs, Kentucky. He graduated magna cum laude from the University of Louisville, Louis D. Brandeis School of Law in 1976. Mr. Morris began his legal career in a defense practice at the law firm of Boehl Stopher Graves & Diendorfer in Louisville, Kentucky, becoming a partner in 1978.

From 1986 to 2007, Doug, along with Louisville attorney Ann Oldfather, grew a law practice focusing primarily on medical malpractice, products liability, pharmaceutical litigation, and complex tort litigation. In 2007, he and Lea Player formed Morris & Player PLLC and together have continued to represent plaintiffs in complex personal injury claims.

Kevin’s practice primarily consists of representing clients in all areas of family law and domestic relations matters, including:

Kevin is passionate about fiercely and effectively representing clients during the difficult transition inherent in divorce and ensuring that each client maintains their dignity, financial security, and promise of a peaceful future both during the divorce process and after divorce through defending and enforcing court orders as necessary.Kevin is an equally fierce advocate for parents who require the legal system to guarantee, protect, defend, and strengthen their relationship with their children in custody and parenting time disputes. Kevin is a demonstrated winner at resolving family law matters through direct litigation and through alternative dispute resolution by way of mediation and Collaborative Law. Kevin’s fundamental focus for your case is not the fight, but getting the outcome tailored to your specific individual needs and desires. Kevin has been a single dad and has personal experience with just how difficult family law cases can be.

Kevin also has a demonstrated history of victory in defending clients accused of crimes at both the state and federal level, although he focuses his defense practice mostly in the state courts of Kentucky and Indiana. Kevin has represented clients across a large range of charges including:

attorneys.name: Liz Mosler
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Liz Mosler is an attorney at the Zoppoth Law Firm. She practices in all areas of employment law, including discrimination, retaliation, sexual harassment, severance agreements, wage and hour violations, workers' compensation, and wrongful termination. Liz also serves the firm's business and commercial litigation clients in Louisville and throughout Kentucky.

Liz has a passion for social justice and civil rights. Prior to joining the Zoppoth Law Firm, Liz was a solo practitioner in Lexington, where she represented employees that had been unlawfully terminated and other individuals facing injustices. Liz also served as the Director of Energy and Environmental policy for a national non-profit organization providing policy analysis to state government officials throughout the country and represented low income individuals and communities as a staff attorney for a Kentucky non-profit organization.

Liz is a Louisville native and earned her B.A. and law degree from the University of Louisville. She has been a licensed attorney since 2008 and is admitted before all Kentucky courts.

In her free time, Liz enjoys spending time with her family, traveling, and mountain biking.

attorneys.name: Kris Douglas Mullins
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Kris Mullins is a lifelong Kentuckian. He was raised in Campbellsville and moved to Lexington in 1994 to attend the University of Kentucky, where he earned both his Bachelor's and Juris Doctorate degrees. He has lived and worked in Lexington ever since.

Mr. Mullins has devoted his entire legal career to representing plaintiffs in medical negligence and other personal injury cases. He opened his own practice with two law school classmates in 2002, and in January 2004 he became a founding member in the firm Savage, Elliott, Houlihan, Moore, Mullins & Erdmann, LLP. He remained a partner with the Savage, Elliott, Houlihan firm until 2012. He operated his own practice briefly in 2012 and 2013 before joining Morgan & Morgan, P.A. in October 2013. His practice continues to focus primarily on medical negligence cases.

Mr. Mullins has received Martindale-Hubbell's "AV" rating, which recognizes lawyers with high ethical standards and professional ability, and according to Martindale-Hubbell, serves as a testament to the fact that Kris' peers rank him at the highest level of professional excellence.

He is married to Melissa Pitt Mullins and has two children, Cooper and Presley.

attorneys.name: Miles D. Mussetter
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
A native of Eastern Kentucky, Miles D. Mussetter is a personal injury attorney driven by a deep commitment to justice and community. He earned his bachelor’s degree in Corporate Finance and Operations & Supply Chain from the nationally ranked Darla Moore School of Business at the University of South Carolina and began his career in corporate logistics. However, it wasn’t long before he became disillusioned with the industry’s focus on profits over people—a realization that inspired him to return home and pursue a law degree at the University of Louisville with the goal of advocating for those harmed by powerful interests.

Miles launched his legal career at a prominent statewide personal injury firm, where he sharpened his litigation skills across a wide range of cases—including motor vehicle and commercial truck accidents, slip and falls, dog bites, civil rights violations, and insurance bad faith. His efforts helped secure substantial, often life-changing results for clients, including multiple seven-figure recoveries throughout Kentucky and neighboring states, excess jury verdicts, and a multi-million-dollar class action settlement against one of the nation’s largest insurers.

In 2024, Miles and his longtime paralegal and case manager, Cynthia Simpson, joined the Bolus Law Office in an of-counsel role. Since joining Bo Bolus and his seasoned team of trial attorneys, Miles and Cynthia have recovered over $10 million on behalf of their clients, continuing their commitment to results-driven, client-centered advocacy.

For Miles, every case is personal. His passion for the law was shaped early on by his father, David Mussetter, a well-respected trial attorney known for his fearless criminal defense work in Eastern Kentucky. Watching his father fight for clients with dignity, integrity, and resolve left a lasting impression—one that Miles now channels in his own legal practice.

Outside the courtroom, Miles enjoys spending time with his wife, Grace, and their infant daughter, Josephine. He is also an active member of his church and remains deeply rooted in the values of faith and family. With a steady hand and a fierce sense of purpose, Miles is proud to stand up for those who need a voice—and to deliver justice with compassion and conviction.

attorneys.name: Lori Fields
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Covington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Lori Fields-Lee graduated magna cum laude with a degree in Political Science from Northern Kentucky University. She then attended Chase College of Law obtaining her law degree in 1983. Lori is licensed in both Kentucky and Ohio and also in the Southern District of Ohio. Her practice takes her to all the Southeast counties in Ohio and all around the Northern counties in Kentucky.

Lori practices extensively with the firm's Real Estate Practice Group. She handles all areas of real estate, both commercial and residential, foreclosure, and homeowner association/condominium law in Kentucky and Ohio.

Lori has served as the Chairperson for the Real Estate Section of the Northern Kentucky Bar Association for four years. She also served as a Board Member of the Northern Kentucky Bar Association.

Lori is involved in golf as her son is a member of the Covington Catholic High School golf team. She also volunteers every year for the Fourth of July festival at Notre Dame Academy. Lori resides in Edgewood, Kentucky with her husband, Gary, and their son.

attorneys.name: A. Nicholas Naiser
attorneys.practice_type: School and Daycare Injuries Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Who I Help

I help Kentucky families who’ve suffered serious injuries or losses – especially in school and daycare incidents, catastrophic vehicle and tractor-trailer crashes, and complex medical malpractice. These cases are hard on good days and overwhelming on bad ones. My role is to steady the process, explain your options in plain English, and fight for a result that helps you rebuild. In almost every case, we’re pursuing the insurance coverage behind the at-fault driver, hospital, or school – not trying to take someone’s personal savings. We make a claim on the policy that exists for exactly this situation, and we hold the insurer to its promises.

How I Work

I build every case like it’s going to trial. That means early investigation, clear timelines, the right experts, and a strategy that’s honest about strengths and weaknesses. If the other side’s insurance company makes a fair offer, we settle. If not, we go to trial. It’s simple, but it’s not easy. Clients get responsive communication and straight talk throughout. Growing up, my grandfather taught me to treat people the way I want to be treated, and I do my best to live up to that every day.

Why This Approach Delivers

Juries respond to credibility and clarity. My results reflect that. At 29, I tried a dental malpractice case by myself and won the highest recorded dental malpractice verdict in Kentucky. But most outcomes aren’t headlines. Because we prepare every case for trial, insurance companies see the risk and pay real value before trial. Many cases resolve confidentially and for significant amounts, often in school injury, trucking, and medical malpractice matters. We keep clients’ details private, use strong experts, and negotiate when the time is right.

Perspective the Defense Respects

After graduating first in my law school class, I began my career defending the same types of cases I file now. I learned how adjusters and defense counsel evaluate exposure, where the pressure points are, and when money really moves. That insight shapes my strategy from day one, helps me anticipate the other side’s arguments, and sets leverage points that move negotiations.

Reputation for Referrals

Most of my work comes by referral. Plaintiff and defense lawyers refer matters to me because they have seen how I work and how I try cases. Former clients recommend me to their circles, and more than once a juror from a prior trial has later hired me for an unrelated issue. That kind of trust is the backbone of my practice.

A Lifelong Louisvillian

I grew up here and never left. I married my college sweetheart, and she’s still my favorite person. We’re raising two awesome kids with help from two very enthusiastic dogs who treat every couch like their own. Our weekends are simple: family time, kids’ practices and games, and a kitchen that never stays clean for long.

Let’s Talk

If something serious happened and you need clear guidance, reach out. Contact us to schedule a free consultation. We can provide a straightforward assessment and a plan for what comes next.

attorneys.name: Michael P. Neal
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Mike began his legal career as a JAG Officer after he was commissioned in the United States Navy in 1990. He served in that role for four year and earned the rank of Lieutenant while enjoying the rich history and beautiful scenery around Pearl Harbor. While in the Navy, Mike was appointed the Special Assistant to the United States Attorney for Honolulu, Hawaii. Mike was able to earn invaluable trial and other litigation experience as he defended the United States from federal tort actions.

Mike had only been in private practice for one year when he joined Pete Sewell in starting this firm in 1995. He now focuses his practice on worker’s compensation defense. He now applies the vigilance expected by the Armed Forces to defending businesses faced with sometimes massive claims for injuries that can have a meaningful impact on the business’s livelihood.

Mike is an avid lover of the outdoors as evidenced by his majoring in Geology and serving on the University of Kentucky’s Journal of Law and Mineral Policy during law school. Mike enjoys hiking, swimming, skiing, and just about any other outdoor activity the Louisville area can offer when he isn’t helping his clients. Mike has also competed in multiple marathons as well as an Ironman Triathlon.

attorneys.name: Kristopher Nevels
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Covington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Kristopher Nevels has been practicing law for over 10 years and concentrating primarily on representing persons injured as a result of negligence. This often includes motor vehicle accidents resulting in personal injury.

Kris began working at Bouldin Law Firm as a law clerk while attending law school at Salmon P. Chase College of Law. He quickly developed a knack for dealing with injured persons and at the same time in negotiating with insurance companies to assure those injured received a fair settlement.

In dealing with injured persons, there often involves investigation of the accident and discussing the case with local police, then making sure the witness information is kept on file in case the case proceeds to litigation. The injured party may have been taken to a hospital and may be in need of additional medical treatment. Whether helping a client to obtain the right treatment or going to a qualified specialist, Kris is in contact and communication with the child to make sure that they are properly treated for their injuries.

Negotiating a fair settlement takes not only years of practice, but a knowledge of what is compensable as well as what both an insurance company and a jury may believe to be a proper resolution. Of course, insurance companies want to pay as little as possible. Whether dealing with PIP/no-fault benefits or dealing with the insurance company for the at-fault party, it is important to know the value of any individual case. This includes jury verdict research as well as handling both simple and complex cases.

attorneys.name: D Sean Nilsen
attorneys.practice_type: construction and commercial litigation Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
D. Sean Nilsen has been a commercial litigator and corporate attorney representing fortune 500 corporations, regional and local companies and individuals throughout his legal career. He has successfully litigated many complex cases and concentrates his practice on construction and commercial litigation, with emphasis on contract disputes, government contracting, construction claims, fidelity and surety law, and commercial transactions.

Prior to the formation of Furman & Nilsen, Sean worked for Woodward, Hobson & Fulton (now Dinsmore & Shohl), a Louisville law firm, handling commercial and construction litigation and corporate matters. Prior to entering law school, Sean owned and operated a structural steel consulting and brokerage firm, working on contract negotiations, design, supply and the supervision of installation techniques for structural steel components used in commercial and industrial construction.

Sean is a 1988 graduate of Arizona State University and a 1992 graduate of the University of Louisville Brandeis School of Law. Sean has lectured and published articles on such topics as recent developments in fidelity and surety law, differing site condition clauses of the Federal Acquisition regulations, construction claims and litigation, mechanics' lien law, termination of federal contractors, design and construction contract defects, and ethical considerations in representing multiple clients in complex litigation. While in law school, Sean also published an article regarding the Age Discrimination and Employment Act.

Sean is licensed to practice in all state and federal courts in Kentucky and Indiana as well as the United States Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States Seventh Circuit court of Appeals. Sean is a member of the Construction and Public Contract Law Section of the Kentucky Bar Association.

Sean is married to Kathleen and when he is not working, he enjoys spending time with her and their five children. They enjoy sports, outdoor activities and working with their youth church organizations.

attorneys.bio:
Mike, a native of West Virginia, began his career as a schoolteacher and pastor before transitioning to law. In 1996, he enrolled in law school, embarking on a new professional path.

Mike specializes in dispute resolution, personal injury defense, premises liability, product liability, and insurance defense. He has extensive experience representing both plaintiffs and defendants in personal injury cases and has worked with individuals, businesses, and insurance companies. As a registered mediator, he has successfully facilitated settlements in Kentucky and Indiana.

With substantial trial experience, Mike has effectively defended companies and individuals in a wide range of personal injury claims, property damage disputes, insurance matters, and subrogation actions. He also has significant experience handling appeals in Kentucky and Indiana.

Mike has represented clients in both state and federal courts across Kentucky and Indiana, achieving successful outcomes at the appellate level in both states.

Outside of his legal practice, Mike enjoys spending time with his wife and two adult children. He is also a certified personal trainer, nutrition coach, and wellness coach.

attorneys.bio:
Paul C. O’Bryan joined Tilford, Dobbins & Schmidt, PLLC in 2022, where he focuses his practice on assisting people in the areas of Probate, Probate litigation, Estate Planning and Family Law. Paul is also a court-approved and certified mediator.

Prior to joining TD&S, Paul spent 21 years with a small Dixie Highway firm gaining experience in drafting simple and complex estate plans, wills, trust, Power of Attorneys, Deeds and contracts. In District Courts, Paul regularly assisted clients with Guardianships, Probate Administration, Will Challenges and other Probate litigation. He prosecuted Divorces, Domestic Violence Orders, Mediation, Custody and Child Support actions as well as Pre-Divorce Mediation in Family Courts. Paul has experience in Circuit Courts with civil litigation and appeals.

Paul has written manuals and lectured on various topics, including the Probate Process and Elder Law to attorneys and other professional groups. Paul has also donated his time and legal services to individuals and groups such as GuardiaCare, the Access Center Partnership and Louisville Bar Association. In his spare time, Paul enjoys spending time with his wife and three daughters (and two dogs!) as well as home renovation projects and mountain biking.

Paul C. O’Bryan joined Tilford, Dobbins & Schmidt, PLLC in 2022, where he focuses his practice on assisting people in the areas of Probate, Probate litigation, Estate Planning and Family Law. Paul is also a court-approved and certified mediator.

Prior to joining TD&S, Paul spent 21 years with a small Dixie Highway firm gaining experience in drafting simple and complex estate plans, wills, trust, Power of Attorneys, Deeds and contracts. In District Courts, Paul regularly assisted clients with Guardianships, Probate Administration, Will Challenges and other Probate litigation. He prosecuted Divorces, Domestic Violence Orders, Mediation, Custody and Child Support actions as well as Pre-Divorce Mediation in Family Courts. Paul has experience in Circuit Courts with civil litigation and appeals.

Paul has written manuals and lectured on various topics, including the Probate Process and Elder Law to attorneys and other professional groups. Paul has also donated his time and legal services to individuals and groups such as GuardiaCare, the Access Center Partnership and Louisville Bar Association. In his spare time, Paul enjoys spending time with his wife and three daughters (and two dogs!) as well as home renovation projects and mountain biking.

attorneys.name: Stephen M. O'Brien, III
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Stephen M. O’Brien, III, grew up in Louisville, Kentucky, where he attended high school at J. M. Atherton High School, graduating in 1965. He attended the University of Virginia, Charlottesville, Virginia and graduated with a B.A. in 1969. He then served two years in the U.S. Army on active duty, completing a tour in the Republic of Vietnam in 1971. He remained in the active reserves in the Army until 1975.

Mr. O’Brien attended the University of Kentucky College of Law, graduating with the degree of Juris Doctor in 1974. He began his practice of law with the firm of McDonald, Alfred & Rosell, where he was an associate from 1974 until 1976. He then joined the firm of Landrum, Patterson & Dickey (now Landrum & Shouse) where he practiced as a trial attorney. He also served as managing partner of the firm for many years. He left Landrum & Shouse in 1993 and began a solo practice in Lexington, representing only those clients who had been injured in some fashion by negligence. His practice included medical negligence, nursing home negligence and products liability.

From 2000 to 2004, he was a partner in the firm of Savage, Garmer, Elliot & O’Brien. From 2004 to 2009, he was a partner in the firm of Garmer & O’Brien. From 2009 to 2017, Mr. O’Brien was the sole partner and owner of the firm of Stephen M. O’Brien, III, PLLC. Since January, 2017, Mr. O’Brien is the senior member of the firm of O'Brien Batten Kirtley & Coomer, PLLC.

Since 1993, Mr. O’Brien’s practice has focused solely on representation of people injured by the negligent acts of others. He is a member of many trial lawyer organizations and is licensed to practice in all courts in Kentucky and is licensed to practice in Florida. He is AV rated by Martindale Hubble. From 2008-2023, he has been recognized as a Super Lawyer. He also serves as an adjunct professor of litigation skills at the University of Kentucky College of Law.

attorneys.name: Derek Patrick O'Bryan
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle & Trucking Accidents Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in Louisville, Kentucky and still call it home. I raised my family here with my wife. After Graduating with Distinction from the University of Kentucky in 1993, I pursued a career outside of the law for several years. Yet, something about practicing law kept beckoning me, and after receiving a scholarship, I enrolled in the Brandeis School of Law at the University of Louisville. In 2003, I graduated Magna Cum Laude and ranked within the top five percent of my class.

After graduation, I spent 9 years representing insurance companies, defending medical malpractice, personal injury, and workers’ compensation cases. Despite working for insurance companies, I maintained a strong sense of empathy for people harmed by the negligence of others, and in 2012, I transitioned to representing their interests.

Now, I only represent individuals who have been harmed by the negligence or illegal actions of others. I have tried numerous cases to verdict and represented clients at hundreds of administrative hearings. Additionally, I have prevailed at all levels of Kentucky Appellate Courts and have several published cases to my name.

I currently focus my practice in the areas of personal injury, workers' compensation, medical malpractice, employment and discrimination law, and general civil litigation. I am admitted to practice law in all courts of the Commonwealth of Kentucky as well as U.S. District Court, Eastern and Western Districts of Kentucky.

Call or e-mail now for a free consultation.

attorneys.name: Shelby Osborne
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Shelby grew up in Lexington, Kentucky. She attended Tates Creek High School in Fayette County. Her mother, Crystal, is a family law attorney in Lexington. In high school, Shelby spent her time working at a local smoothie shop and playing on her high school golf team. She was team MVP of the girls’ golf team her senior year.

After high school, Shelby went to the University of Kentucky to continue her academic career. She majored in political science and minored in biology and French. She studied abroad on Semester at Sea, where she traveled to eleven different countries. She was also a member of Kappa Kappa Gamma and spent her free time volunteering with the Lexington Humane Society.

After graduating from undergrad, Shelby went on to attend the University of Kentucky College of Law, where she was a member of the Women’s Law Caucus. After law school, Shelby moved to Omaha, Nebraska, to work for a national title insurance company. After a few years, Shelby decided to move home and began working for a large Kentucky firm, doing real estate transactions. Then she decided to switch practice areas and started working for a national personal injury firm in their Lexington office. She has represented individuals across the state in a variety of matters, conducting numerous depositions, oral arguments, and mediations. In her spare time, she enjoys spending time with friends, family, and her two rescue dogs and cat. Shelby is very excited to join the team at Hicks & Funfsinn, PLLC!

attorneys.name: Gracie J. Ovington
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Gracie J. Ovington, née Davis, grew up in Scott County, Kentucky. She received her Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies and History, Summa Cum Laude, from Morehead State University, and Juris Doctor, Summa Cum Laude, from the University of Louisville, Brandeis School of Law.

While at Morehead, Ovington founded and served as the first president of the Women in Law club. She also worked as the Student Coordinator of the Pro Se Divorce Clinic, a collaboration between the Legal Studies Department and Legal Aid of the Bluegrass.

Prior to attending law school, Ovington interned with the Commonwealth Attorney’s office and clerked at Hicks & Funfsinn, a personal injury firm.

At Brandeis, Ovington interned with Federal Magistrate Judge Regina Edwards. She also was a student instructor through the Central High Street Law program, research assistant, teaching assistant, and member of the Human Rights Advocacy Program. Ovington served as an Articles Editor for the University of Louisville Law Review for Volume 63. She began her time at Strause Law Group as a law clerk while a student at Brandeis.

As an Associate Attorney at Strause Law Group, Ovington is honored to represent clients in a broad range of legal matters, including Professional Licensure Defense, Business Transactions and Disputes, Healthcare Law, Employment Law, and Contracts.

Outside of the office, she enjoys time with friends and family, arts and crafts, and reading.

attorneys.name: James O’Toole
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
James N. O'Toole is the Managing Partner of O'Toole & Williams Law. He has served as a trusted legal advisor for business owners and individuals since 1995 with clients ranging from individuals and small businesses to $800M conglomerates.

Mr. O'Toole prides himself on taking the time to fully understand his client's needs and formulating an effective plan to accomplish his client's goals. By investing himself fully in understanding the client's situation Mr. O'Toole determines how best to help them. With a wealth of experience in estate planning, family law, criminal defense, personal and property damage claims, and employment matters, James prides himself on handling personal matters with compassion and understanding.

Mr. O'Toole was immersed in the highly competitive automotive supplier battlefield from his first days as an attorney. Providing legal counsel to individuals, manufacturers, machine tool builders and sales and marketing companies gave Mr. O'Toole a well-rounded understanding of the diverse needs of different clients.

There is a common thread that runs through every matter handled by Mr. O'Toole - the client comes to him in their time of need for help with a problem they can't handle on their own. Over the years, and through the experience of battles from the boardroom to the courtroom, as well as planning to avoid those battles, Mr. O'Toole has learned that keeping an open mind, listening, and learning from the client produces the best results.

If you would like to contact Mr. O'Toole directly he can be reached at jotoole@OWLawky.com

attorneys.bio:
Heather Pack Howell recently joined our Lexington office, bringing with her 18 years of experience handling personal injury cases. She is an Eastern Kentucky native and a 1995 graduate of Prestonsburg High School. She received her B.A. in Political Science and Psychology, magna cum laude, from the University of Kentucky in 2000 and her law degree from the University of Kentucky College of Law in 2003.

Following her graduation from law school, Heather worked for a general practice law firm for more than a decade. During that time she represented injured parties in both motor vehicle accidents and premises liability cases. In 2015, she shifted her practice to personal injury defense, where she remained until joining our firm as a Lexington accident attorney in August 2021. Her invaluable experience as a Lexington injury attorney has proven to be a great strength in helping injured parties navigate and resolve their claims with insurance companies.

Heather is a member of the Kentucky Bar Association, Fayette County Bar Association, University of Kentucky Alumni Association, and United Commercial Travelers of America. She is AV Preeminent Peer Rated for the Highest Level of Professional Excellence.

Heather resides in Lexington, Kentucky with her daughters, Abby and Kylie, who keep her busy outside of the office with their various athletic endeavors.

attorneys.name: Bradley R. Palmer
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Bradley R. Palmer was born, raised, and educated right here in Louisville. After graduating from DuPont Manual High School, he attended the University of Louisville, earning degrees in Political Science and History in 2006, and completing a dual J.D./M.A. Political Science degree program through the Brandeis School of Law in 2010. In law school, Brad was a member and editor of the Journal of Law and Education, and an Academic Fellow. Brad has been with Conliffe, Sandmann & Sullivan, starting as a law clerk and later as an associate, since May 2009. Since that time, he has successfully prosecuted and defended civil cases in several areas including:

Construction Litigation:

Worked with owners of properties and projects ranging from eight-figure commercial, industrial, and recreational facilities, to multi- and single-family residential builds, on everything from contract drafting and negotiation, to in-project consulting and guidance, to advancing claims against contractors, manufacturers and bond sureties for incomplete or defective work, to defending owners against various contractor claims for additional pay.

Represented general contractors in payment disputes with both owners and subcontractors, and pursued claims against subcontractors and suppliers for improper or untimely performance.

Represented contractors and subcontractors in filing mechanic’s liens for unpaid work, resolving disputes with owners over change orders and costly inefficiencies, and enforcing contractor rights under the Kentucky Fairness in Construction Act.

Employment Litigation:

Defended municipal and private entities against claims of discrimination/retaliation based on race, age, disability, and worker’s comp filings, winning summary judgments in multiple cases.

Participated in successful prosecution of sexual harassment claims, unemployment hearings, wage and hour claims, and employment contract claims, while also representing employers and employees in crafting, enforcing, and/or defending non-compete agreements, non-solicitation agreements, and other post-employment terms and conditions.

Business and Commercial:

Assisted businesses large and small in start-up consulting and crafting company formation documents, maintaining compliance with filing requirements, and coaching best practices for business governance and recordkeeping.

Represented businesses, business owners, and business partners in various disputes, ranging from breaches of contract, to illegal inference with business relations, to violation of fiducial obligations between partners, to misappropriation and mismanagement damaging the interests of limited investors and minority partners

Acted as local counsel for the preparation and filing of mortgages, fixture filings and other land records on behalf of out-of-state and foreign business ventures.

Brad also has experience with several other areas of civil practice, prosecuting securities fraud and suitability claims, litigation associated with partnership, LLC, and non-profit business transitions and dissolutions, UCC issues (warranties, negotiable instruments, letters of credit, and secured transactions),, and insurance coverage disputes (CGL, Builder’s Risk, UM/UIM). He can also help you with basic estate planning, will preparation, and probate administration.

attorneys.name: William Pauley Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
When you are dealing with a family law matter, having an experienced and compassionate advocate on your side can make a meaningful difference. William “Bill” Pauley is a Senior Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm, proudly serving clients from the firm’s Lexington, Kentucky office. He is dedicated to helping individuals and families navigate challenging legal situations with professionalism, understanding, and care.

Bill earned his Juris Doctor from the Salmon P. Chase College of Law at Northern Kentucky University, where he received the Commonwealth Scholarship for full tuition. He completed his Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at Transylvania University in Lexington, Kentucky.

Bill brings more than two decades of diverse legal experience to his role at Stange Law Firm. Before joining the Lexington, KY divorce and family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Bill most recently served as a Housing Justice Attorney with the Kentucky Equal Justice Center, where he represented tenants in eviction proceedings under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act. In this role, he advocated for housing stability and worked to secure favorable outcomes for clients facing difficult circumstances.

Throughout his career, Bill has served in several key legal and leadership roles across Kentucky. As General Counsel to the Kentucky Senate Democratic Leadership, he analyzed legislation for constitutional compliance and provided legal recommendations to Senate leadership. He also served as a Staff Attorney for the Kentucky Department for Local Government, where he advised municipalities on statutory compliance, procurement, and governance, drafted administrative regulations for the state’s $250 million Broadband Deployment Fund, and provided legal support to the Kentucky Infrastructure Authority.

Earlier in his career, Bill worked as General Counsel and Compliance Officer for PremierTox, Inc., where he oversaw HR operations and regulatory compliance during a period of significant organizational growth. He also maintained a solo practice, representing clients in family law, property disputes, and guardianship cases. Bill began his legal career as a Staff Attorney with the Kentucky Department of Public Advocacy, where he defended indigent clients in district and circuit courts and participated in Drug Court and Teen Court initiatives.

In addition to his extensive legal experience, Bill has been active in professional and community organizations. He is a former President of the Municipal Law Section of the Kentucky Bar Association, has served on the Fiscal Services Committee for the Ronald McDonald House of the Bluegrass, and has volunteered with the Scott County Drug Court and Teen Court programs.

With his long-standing dedication to public service and broad experience across multiple areas of law, Bill approaches each case with empathy, diligence, and a focus on achieving positive outcomes for his clients. Whether guiding individuals through divorce, custody disputes, or other family law matters, he is committed to providing skilled and compassionate representation every step of the way.

attorneys.name: Sean Pharr
attorneys.practice_type: Trial Practice Lawyers in Fort Mitchell, KY
attorneys.bio:
I am the lead attorney and founder of the Pharr Law Group. I have dedicated my career to defending people in the state and federal courts all around the Commonwealth of Kentucky, specializing in complex criminal cases. I also regularly represent individuals charged with misdemeanors, traffic offenses, and in certain family court matters.

I completed my undergraduate education at the University of Kentucky with degrees in Philosophy and Political Science. I graduated from the Salmon P. Chase College of Law with the highest honors while serving as Executive Editor of the Northern Kentucky Law Review and competing in multiple national competitions in mock trial and appellate advocacy.

After law school, I moved to Louisville for the only legal position I have ever applied for: as a trial lawyer with the Louisville Metro Public Defender. There I learned true, indiscriminate passion and gained invaluable experience defending thousands of cases ranging from DUI to Murder on behalf of those who could not afford a lawyer. I tried many cases as a public defender and won more awards for full acquittals in felony jury trials than any of the other 75 lawyers during my time at the office. I also served as Deputy Division Chief, a leadership role over a team of trial lawyers with added responsibilities to train office staff on a range of topics. While a public defender, I am proud to have graduated from the prestigious National Criminal Defense College in Macon, Georgia. I will forever be a public defender at heart and regularly accept appointments representing indigent clients in both the state and federal courts.

I founded my private practice in 2017 in Louisville shortly before moving home to Northern Kentucky to start a family. With deep ties to both places, my practice naturally bridged both areas. Over time, as I represented clients from both locations and their surrounding areas, the courts in which I regularly practiced gradually expanded. Today, I have defended felony cases in nearly 80 of Kentucky’s 120 counties.

As an active member of the Kentucky Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, I continue working tirelessly to master the craft of criminal defense. My philosophy is simple: I do not care what my clients may or may not have done. I will not leave this office, or take my seat in court, until every person I represent receives the same level of defense that I would demand for my own family.

sections.title: Representative Cases
content: Citation: When police claimed our client had caused a fatal head-on collision while under the influence, he was charged with DUI and Murder, facing life in prison. Despite having fled an accident scene littered with opened alcohol containers, Sean secured the client’s pretrial release while he challenged the government’s evidence and enlisted the help of a renowned accident reconstructionist. On the eve of trial, we were able to negotiate probation on reduced charges avoiding all prison time.

Citation: Our client’s nightmare had only just begun when his 4-week-old son stopped breathing in his arms. Doctors found bleeding on the baby’s brain and fractures in multiple parts of his body. After the region’s preeminent forensic pediatrician issued a devastating report that the injuries were intentionally inflicted by our client, he was charged and faced 10 years in prison. By meticulously investigating the child’s whereabouts for every day of his young life, and raising substantial medical questions about whether the injuries were caused by a stroke in the womb, Sean was able to negotiate a resolution which would have eventually dismissed the charges. But our client persisted in his innocence and rejected the offer. After a taxing week-long trial, our client was exonerated and reunited with his son after nearly 2 years.

Citation: It was a tragedy caught on tape at a bar, as our client raised a 45 caliber pistol to a man’s chest and shot him at close range. The two were friends, and while the man lived, he will likely never walk again. Refusing to believe our client never meant to pull the trigger, the government charged him with Attempted Murder and Assault. After a years-long legal battle, the case culminated in a trial that amounted to a legal dissertation on the concept of intent. When the jury announced that it had ac

Citation: In a recent case, our client was pulled over on suspicion of DUI. Although she admitted to drinking, had an open bottle of wine in the car, and “failed” the field sobriety tests (according to officer), she gave us enough to work with by refusing the breath test. With his client’s nursing license on the line, Sean tried the case. The jury deliberated just 10 minutes before returning a verdict of Not Guilty.

Citation: Absolutely nobody (not even us at first) believed our client, with a long history of drug trafficking, possessed a substantial quantity of narcotics for mere personal use. But after a year of litigation, many “spirited” confrontations with prosecutor and judge alike, and some teaching about the value, quantity, and business of this particular drug, Sean helped his client avoid a 20-year sentence. We are thrilled in knowing that our client successfully completed probation and is now 5 years clean and sober.

attorneys.firm_name: Michael J. Thompson, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Oak Grove, KY
attorneys.bio:
James Phillips (Of counsel)

James Phillips is a member of the American Bar Association and the Tennessee Bar Association. He is also a member of the Tennessee Trial Lawyer's Association. He has been admitted to practice in Tennessee and in the United States District Court for Middle Tennessee.

As an Attorney in the Middle District of Tennessee, James has represented numerous divorce and family law clients. He recently represented Country Singer Terry Clark's husband in their Davidson County divorce. He also represents criminal clients and has handled cases ranging from Murder and Rape to simple public intox.

As a military law attorney, while stationed at Fort Campbell as an Army JAG, James served in Operation Iraqi Freedom with the 101st Airborne Division (AASLT) and spent three years at the Fort Campbell Office of the Staff Judge Advocate. He has proudly served as the “Strike" - Second Brigade Combat Team- Trial Counsel, represented more than a thousand clients in his capacity as a Legal Assistance Attorney and Chief of Legal Assistance. At the end of his military career, James was assigned to Trial Defense Services as a Defense Counsel at the Fort Campbell Office for Trial Defense Services Region III. He has also represented numerous clients as a Civilian Defense Counsel.

James graduated from Vanderbilt Law School in May 2001. While at Vanderbilt, he interned with the Nashville Metro District Attorney's Office. He also successfully represented social security clients at administrative hearings while a member of the Vanderbilt Civil Legal Aid Clinic.

Among his other accomplishments, James led the effort to establish the Mosul Office of Judicial Operation (MOJO) in April 2003 in Mosul, Iraq. His office, consisting of two Iraqi Attorneys, two military attorneys and two paralegals, tracked detainee operations and initiated the rebuilding of the Iraqi Judicial System in Northern Iraq. He was awarded a Bronze Star for his efforts in Iraq.

He is currently licensed as an Attorney in both Tennessee and Montana. He is a graduate of the Judge Advocates Officer Basic Course, Airborne School and the Primary Leadership Development Course.

Finally, as a former sergeant with the 18th Airborne Corps Artillery out of Fort Bragg, James is a veteran of the Gulf War. He fondly remembers being a single enlisted soldier.

attorneys.name: Zack D. Phillips
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Zack is a dedicated and highly motivated legal professional with Bar admissions in Kentucky and Tennessee and a Juris Doctor from the University of Kentucky College of Law (2023). His academic and practical achievements reflect his commitment to a career in law and public service.

During his time at the University of Kentucky, Zack actively engaged in extracurricular activities, serving as a member of both the Moot Court Board and Trial Advocacy Board. Notably, he was a Competition Committee Member and a 2023 Garmer Cup Competition Finalist. While at UK, Zack started volunteering at the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program helping members of underserved communities prepare and file their taxes. He has continued to volunteer with the clinic ever since.

As an Ohio native, Zack's educational background includes a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Kent State University (2019), with a focus on Public Policy. His outstanding performance earned him a place on the Dean's List and membership in the National Political Science Honor Society (Pi Sigma Alpha).

Zack began his legal career as a Law Clerk for the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government, furthering his understanding of municipal law before transitioning into civil litigation and insurance defense. After some time gaining practical insight on the art of litigating, Zack transitioned into transactional legal work as a Real Estate, Estate Planning and Administration Attorney before finding his passion in Employment Law at Spitz, The Employee's Law Firm.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Lea Player is a member of the law firm of Morris & Player, PLLC, a plaintiffs' professional malpractice and catastrophic personal injury practice in Louisville, KY. Lea's drive to seek justice for the disadvantaged caused her to seek her first legal job at the Jefferson County Public Defenders' Office while she was still in law school. That same desire to help people has persisted for the last 25 years. It fuels the law practice of Morris & Player. After graduating U of L law school in 1992, Lea developed her litigation skills defending mass tort and complex litigation cases such as the civil litigation that arose out of the Oklahoma City bombing, thousands of breast implant lawsuits and similar products liability cases. When she began representing injured clients over fifteen years ago, Lea found that the litigation skills she had developed in the complex litigation arena made her a formidable advocate in personal injury cases, from medical malpractice to workplace injuries to catastrophic truck and auto accidents. In 2007, she and Doug Morris formed the firm of Morris & Player PLLC where together they continue to represent plaintiffs in complex cases, cases involving catastrophic injuries and professional malpractice.

attorneys.name: Debra S. Pleatman
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Covington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Debbie Pleatman is a native of Cincinnati, Ohio. Debbie is admitted to practice in Kentucky, Ohio, and the District of Columbia. She graduated from the University of Cincinnati with a Bachelor's in Business Administration (BBA). After working in retail management, Debbie graduated from the Northern Kentucky University, Salmon P. Chase College of Law (JD).

Debbie has worked at Ziegler & Schneider, P.S.C. since 1992. She is a partner with the firm and concentrates her practice in civil litigation. She has worked in many matters, including, but not limited to, construction disputes, contract disputes, collection, and landlord-tenant issues. Debbie also handles matters involving all types of family law. Debbie has worked on dissolution of long-term marriages and short-term marriages. She has handled issues involving children, parenting time, grandparent visitation, child support, and many other facets of domestic law.

Debbie currently serves on the Ethics Committee of the Kentucky Bar Association. She also serves the Kentucky Bar Association as a member of the Hotline Committee. As a Hotline Committee member, she assists attorneys with ethical questions which may arise in the course of their client representation. Debbie is a Life Fellow of the Kentucky Bar Foundation, serves on the Board of the Northern Kentucky Volunteer Lawyers, Inc., and is on the volunteer panel for Legal Aid of the Bluegrass.

She and her husband, Greg Frank, live in Villa Hills, Kentucky, and between the two of them have raised 3 daughters.

attorneys.name: Scott E. Powell
attorneys.practice_type: Birth Injuries Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Scott Powell is a dynamic trial lawyer and negotiator who has recovered millions of dollars for his clients. Scott's practice consists of cases involving catastrophic injury and/or death stemming from motor vehicle negligence, medical negligence, and corporate wrongdoing.

Scott also serves as an adjunct professor at the Louis D. Brandeis School of Law at the University of Louisville, where he teaches negotiation theory and technique to upper level law students.

Scott began his career representing insurance and health care companies, often helping defend doctors and hospitals. His early success prompted him to leave a prominent defense firm at age 30 to start his own firm dedicated to representing individuals. That firm, now Powell Klausing PLLC, relies on its intimate knowledge of the insurance and health care industries to help clients obtain maximum awards for their injuries.

Since becoming a plaintiff's lawyer, Scott has been named a Top 100 Trial Lawyer by The National Trial Lawyers organization, and has designated a 'SuperLawyer' by Thomson Reuters, a status bestowed upon less than 5% of all lawyers. In addition, Scott has been featured in publications such as Attorney at Law Magazine, Forbes, and Bloomberg Businessweek.

While in law school, Scott was a national champion moot court negotiator and represented the U.S. in international competition. In addition, Scott served as a legal intern for the U.S. Commercial Attache office of the London Embassy, where he helped American companies doing business in Europe.

attorneys.name: Jerome P. Prather
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Jay Prather is a partner at Garmer & Prather. He is committed to the representation of clients who have been seriously injured, have been the victim of a workplace wrong, or whose rights have been adversely affected.

Jay is an adjunct professor at the University of Kentucky David J. Rosenberg College of Law, where he teaches an upper-level course in medical liability. He has been recognized by his peers. He is rated AV-Preeminent® by the Martindale-Hubbell* peer review, the highest rating an attorney can receive, and is currently listed as a Kentucky Super Lawyer, and for six years before that he was listed as a Super Lawyers Rising Star. Jay is a District Vice President of the Kentucky Justice Association, and has been a member of the Board of Governors since 2011. He has also been selected to the American Inns of Court. Jay is one of a small number of lawyers under the age of 40 who has argued cases before both the Kentucky Supreme Court and the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. He was been called on to testify before the Kentucky Senate Judiciary Committee about the effect of proposed legislation that would have limited the Attorney General's ability to contract with lawyers on a contingency fee basis. He also serves the profession by regularly leading and appearing on the faculty of various continuing legal education seminars for other lawyers.

Jay earned his Bachelor of Arts from Vanderbilt University with a double major in economics and political science. He is a 2006 graduate of the University of Kentucky College of Law. At UK, he was named Outstanding Third-Year Staff Member of the Kentucky Law Journal and was a member of the Moot Court Board. He was also a member of the Environmental Law Society, Student Public Interest Law Foundation, and American Constitution Society.

Jay is admitted to practice in all state and federal courts in Kentucky. He has also been admitted to practice pro hac vice in Ohio, Tennessee, and Alabama. He is a member of the American, Kentucky, and Fayette County Bar Associations, the Federal Bar Association, the Kentucky Justice Association, and the American Association for Justice. Jay is a Life Fellow of the Kentucky Bar Foundation.

Jay lives in Lexington, with his wife, young son, and adopted golden retriever. He is an active member and vice-moderator of the congregation at Crestwood Christian Church, and is a volunteer for Habitat for Humanity and the Vanderbilt Alumni Association. He is a former editor-in-chief of Vanderbilt University's Orbis, a former chairman of Habitat for Humanity’s Vanderbilt University Campus Chapter, and an Eagle Scout. He has been with the firm since he began as a law clerk in 2004.

*Martindale-Hubbell is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings™ fall into two categories - legal ability and general ethical standards. AV®, BV®, AV Preeminent® and BV Distinguished® are registered certification marks of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used under in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies.

attorneys.name: Tony Prieto
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Claims Lawyers in Louisville, KY
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Tampa, Mr. Prieto graduated from Tampa Catholic High School in 1993. Soon thereafter, Mr. Prieto received a Bachelor of Arts in English Literature with a minor in Criminology from Florida State University.

Mr. Prieto attended Stetson University College of Law where he completed a State Judicial Internship before receiving his Juris Doctor Degree in 1999. Upon graduation, Mr. Prieto worked as a State Prosecutor for Hillsborough County under Harry Lee Coe and Mark Ober, prosecuting cases ranging from criminal traffic violations to major drug offenses.

Subsequent to his tenure as a prosecutor, Mr. Prieto joined the law firm of Prieto, Prieto, & Goan where he successfully defended criminal matters, as well as, represented countless injured clients as the result of negligence. Mr. Prieto was the managing partner of the First Party Litigation Department that encompassed disputes arising from insurance companies' refusal to properly reimburse insurance benefits on behalf of their insureds.

Throughout his legal career, Mr. Prieto has been lead counsel on countless trials involving both civil and criminal matters. Today, Mr. Prieto is employed in the First Party Litigation Department of Morgan & Morgan where he represents the interest of thousands of insureds across Florida.

Mr. Prieto is admitted and qualified as an attorney before The Florida Bar and The U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida.

Mason Proffitt joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele in 2018 as an associate in the firm’s Lexington, Kentucky office. Practicing primarily in Workers’ Compensation Defense, Mason is a member of the firm’s Civil Litigation department.

Originally from a small rural town near Bowling Green, Kentucky, Mason attended Western Kentucky University where he graduated in 2013 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science. Upon graduation, Mason moved to Lexington, Kentucky, to attend University of Kentucky College of Law. While earning his Juris Doctor, Mason was a board member on the University’s moot court team; he also served as a judicial intern and extern in Fayette County Family Court. After graduating law school in 2016 and successfully passing the Kentucky bar exam, Mason joined a small civil litigation firm in London, Kentucky, practicing primarily insurance defense.

Mason currently lives in Lexington, Kentucky, and enjoys going to the gym, live music, and bartending private events.

attorneys.bio:
An Experienced Lawyer Fighting For You Who Never Quits

James C. Puszczewicz is an attorney with over a decade of courtroom experience handling personal injury and criminal defense cases. With more than 10 years of experience, attorney James C. Puszczewicz Jim offers clients confident, effective representation and is not afraid to fight for their rights. Located in Louisville, Kentucky, Mr. Puszczewicz has previous experience in insurance defense and has witnessed firsthand how people like you were left with nothing during hard times. Whether you have suffered injuries due to the negligence of others or are facing serious criminal charges or have suffered injuries to the negligence of others, his firm ZZZ Legal will we will protect your rights and work to get you the results you deserve.

Jim is the youngest son of a large Polish family originally from Chicago. He has lived in various parts of the United States including Chicago, Iowa, Florida and Kentucky. As a high school student he was a two-time state debate champion who went on to debate in college on scholarship. In law school he was a two-time moot court national champion. Prior to going into law he had worked in a variety of jobs such as landscaping and golf course maintenance, in construction as a mason's assistant and with his family in a retail produce company. As an attorney he has diverse experience as a trial lawyer. He began as a public defender and handled a large caseload of serious and challenging criminal cases. He learned civil practice first as an insurance defense personal injury lawyer where he gained invaluable experience which taught him how the insurance company acts to defend your case. He also later worked with a reputable and high profile personal injury firm handling everything from minor injury cases to major medical malpractice and class action lawsuits.

Jim uses this diverse background and experience to serve ZZZ Legal's clients with personal attention, aggressive legal representation and the legal "know how" to get results for you. He enjoys the personal relationships and trust he forms with his clients. He enjoys making a difference in his client's lives and he thrives on the competitive nature of the adversarial legal system. He tireless efforts on behalf of his client's has earned him the bulldog reputation. Call now - don't wait to unleash the bulldog on your case!

attorneys.name: Jonathan Rabinowitz
attorneys.practice_type: Entertainment Law Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan Rabinowitz serves as the Managing Partner for the firm's five Kentucky offices, two Indiana offices and its West Virginia office. In addition to his duties as Managing Partner, he devotes a substantial portion of his practice to catastrophic personal injury cases, wrongful death claims, complex litigation and complex governmental actions. Mr. Rabinowitz has been honored with the prestigious "AV Rating" by Martindale Hubbell. The rating is based upon evaluations by other lawyers and is the highest ranking attainable for an attorney for ability and ethics in the practice of law.

Mr. Rabinowitz graduated Magna Cum Laude from Newberry College where he played football and was Student Body President. Thereafter, he obtained his Juris Doctor from the University of Louisville School of Law, where he was Torts Editor of the Journal of Law and Education. During law school, he also had the privilege of clerking with then Senate President David Williams. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Rabinowitz was a Partner in a law firm that represented insurance carriers in State and Federal Courts throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky.

In April of 2020 Mr. Rabinowitz was appointed by Governor Beshear as Chairman of the Kentucky Horse Racing Commission. He was also named the Chair of the Kentucky Horsemen Race Date Committee. Prior to that time Mr. Rabinowitz was appointed to Governor Beshear's Transition Team for the Public Protection Cabinet.

Mr. Rabinowitz is married to Kathleen Kelly Rabinowitz with whom he as 3 children: Caroline, Madelynn and Charlotte.

attorneys.name: William C. Rambicure
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Commercial Law Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Bill is admitted to practice law in all state courts in the Commonwealth of Kentucky, in the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Kentucky, the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court. He has briefed and presented oral arguments to the Kentucky Court of Appeals, Kentucky Supreme Court, and the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals. Bill is a member of the Kentucky Bar Association (“KBA”) and the Fayette County Bar Association (“FCBA”). He has served as an officer and director of the FCBA (including secretary, treasurer, vice president, and president) and as an officer and director of the FCBA Pro Bono Program, Inc.

Throughout his 40 plus years practicing law, Bill has been involved in an extensive, varied, and diverse civil litigation practice. He has experience in representing both plaintiffs and defendants in personal and commercial litigation matters including pre-judgment and post-judgment collection matters, foreclosures, replevins. writs of possession, garnishments, attachments, temporary restraining orders, temporary or permanent injunctions, etc.). Bill has experience in handling adversary proceedings in bankruptcy court, having recently represented a large Kentucky based coal company’s officers and directors in the defense of bankruptcy court adversary proceedings for alleged breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duties, negligence, and various and sundry other tort based claims.

He has represented both plaintiffs and defendants and/or their insurers) in residential and commercial environmental clean-up and remediation claims and has represented claimants in connection with bad faith and unfair claims settlement practices claims. He has also represented plaintiffs in various lender liability claims relating to personal and/or commercial loan transactions.

Additionally, Bill is a skilled mediator with experience providing an effective alternative to extended litigation. https://www.kentuckyadr.com/

attorneys.name: Virginia M. Riggs
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Marvin Knorr & Associates
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Covington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Virginia is a life-long resident of Northern Kentucky. She is the daughter of a Peruvian immigrant whose mother raised her by herself after her father passed away when she was five years old. She became a lawyer to help people. On the first day of law school, her professor asked, how many of you are here to simply make money in a corporate setting and how many of you are here to serve the public and help people. Out of the 120 students in that class, she was one of only five people who raised their hand to serve the public and help people. Virginia represents her clients diligently with a great degree of compassion and care. She advocates aggressively for her clients with a desire to serve the best interests of children. She has a vast array of clients from every socio-economic and demographic background.

Virginia graduated from Salmon P. Chase College of Law in 2007 with her Juris Doctor and cum laude honors. While in law school, she was a member of the trial advocacy team and interned for the Campbell County Commonwealth Attorney's Office. attorneys.name: Ryan Roark
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
My journey to becoming an attorney was shaped by watching firsthand how the law can positively impact people's lives. Growing up in Versailles, Kentucky, as the son of an employment attorney, I witnessed daily how skilled legal advocacy could help people through their most challenging moments. While I didn't always know I wanted to be a lawyer, seeing my father's fulfilling work helping others eventually drew me to the profession.

Sports and teamwork were fundamental parts of my early life. Throughout high school, I competed in basketball, baseball, and golf, learning valuable lessons about dedication and collaboration that I now bring to my legal practice. This team-oriented mindset led me to join the Kentucky National Guard, where I served as an Infantryman from 2015 to 2021. My military service taught me discipline, leadership, and the importance of standing up for others – skills that prove invaluable in my legal career.

After earning my BS in Business and Economics from the University of Kentucky, I pursued my law degree at UK's J. David Rosenberg College of Law during the challenging years of 2020-2023. I graduated in the top third of my class and served as a staff editor for the Kentucky Law Journal. During this time, I also authored a publication examining the constitutionality of Kentucky's slot machines.

My legal experience was enriched by clerking for the Honorable Judge Samuel Todd Spalding and working as a summer associate at Phillips Parker Orberson & Arnett, PLC in Louisville. These experiences helped shape my understanding of how to effectively advocate for clients while navigating the complexities of the legal system.

Today, I'm proud to practice alongside my father and Tyler at Roark & Korus, PLLC, where we share a commitment to representing both employees and employers in employment disputes. This unique perspective allows me to better serve our clients and work toward fair resolutions that make a real difference in people's lives.

Outside of practicing law, you'll find me pursuing my passion for endurance sports, golf, or cheering on my beloved Bengals and Kentucky Wildcats. These things help maintain the balance and perspective that I bring to my legal practice every day.

My goal is simple: to help people navigate through challenging times while achieving the justice they deserve. Whether representing an employee facing workplace discrimination or helping a business resolve complex employment issues, I'm committed to providing the dedicated advocacy our clients need to move forward.

attorneys.name: Robert L. Roark Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Disputes Lawyers in Lexington, KY
attorneys.bio:
Rob was born and raised in Central Kentucky and attended the University of Kentucky for both his undergraduate and law degrees. While in law school, Rob was a member of the UK Law Journal.

Since graduating from law school in 1989, Rob has dedicated his practice to resolving employment disputes for Kentucky employees and employers. Rob handles cases in state and federal courts throughout Kentucky, including a history of successful appellate practice in both state and federal courts, including the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals. Rob is also admitted to practice before the United States Supreme Court.

Rob has obtained jury verdicts and numerous judgments for businesses and individuals in state and federal courts, including a recent six-figure jury verdict on behalf of a single plaintiff in Richmond, Kentucky, who the jury determined had been terminated in retaliation for becoming injured on the job. Rob takes pride in the fact that he also assists businesses in resolving their employment law issues. By representing both employees and employers, Rob brings a unique, insightful perspective that he zealously uses in the representation of his clients.

Rob has successfully represented both employees and employers in discrimination, whistleblower, and wage and hour cases, both individually and in class and collective actions, including under the Kentucky Civil Rights Act, Title VII, FMLA, and the FLSA.
